data.title: As students protest, how dilapidated really are France's school buildings?
data.description: As France's student protest movement continues, one of the main grievances is the conditions of the country’s schools, with many buildings severely dilapidated and in some cases, facing dangerous risks. data.title: Japan holds first ‘competitive sleeping’ contest
data.description: Sleep deprivation is seen these days as a major health issue - not least of all in Japan where people sleep less on average than in any other OECD country. Now, a new contest for "competitive sleepers" is hoping to encourage people to snooze for longer. The Tokyo competition, dubbed "Matt Race", saw dozens of participants fitted with sleep tracking devices sprawl on comfy mattresses to slumber for up to 90 minutes Monday, competing for the top prize of over two million yen ($14,000).

data.title: A medieval manuscript has confounded scholars for centuries. Have they been reading it wrong all this time?
data.description: Researchers argue incorrect binding of Voynich manuscript radically changes ideas about its drawings and indecipherable text It has been called the world’s most mysterious manuscript: a medieval set of pages filled with botanical drawings, astronomical diagrams, pictures of nude women and indecipherable text. Claimed at various times to be a book in a lost language, a musical score, an instruction manual or just an elaborate hoax, the so-called Voynich manuscript’s true meaning has defied cryptographers and codebreakers for centuries. Now, new research offers an explanation for why a scholarly consensus over this enduring puzzle has been so hard to come by: not only because its truth is so profoundly mysterious – but because everyone has been reading its pages in the wrong order. data.title: ‘It could knock a whole street down’: the art of defusing a second world war bomb
data.description: On 14 January this year, army and navy squads faced an unprecedented challenge: one bomb on a Plymouth building site, another floating on a dredger in Exmouth. That afternoon, the clock started ticking Everyone at Exmouth Marina knew there was an unexploded German bomb in the water. Old hands at the dock had been saying so since the end of the second world war. But the marina had been dredged and re-dredged and nothing had ever come up. It had started to sound like an old wives’ tale. The marina is a busy stretch of water: a commercial port until the late 1990s that had since been converted into a home to private yachts. A bomb, you’d think, would have a hard time staying hidden. But in the middle of the afternoon on Wednesday 14 January 2026, 81 years after the end of the second world war, Steve Hockings-Thompson, the manager of Exmouth Marina, got a call from the crew of a dredging vessel telling him he’d better come out to the boat. “I thought: ‘Oh crikey. We’ve got a bit of an issue here,’” Hockings-Thompson told me recently. He went out to the dredger, a squat barge that hauls silt and other debris from the marina floor on to a flat deck that resembles a steel sieve. Sitting on the deck was a huge hunk of metal, caked in mud and stones. As Hockings-Thompson got closer and saw its distinctive conical shape, he knew it was a bomb – a big one. The dredger was loaded with 20,000 litres of diesel fuel, so if the bomb detonated, it would be disastrous. He called the police, who quickly came to the scene. “And then,” he said, “all hell broke loose.” Continue reading...

data.title: The 90s: Art and Fashion review – this isn’t an exhibition, it’s a magazine spread
data.description: Tate Britain, London The Young British Art of the 1990s was brash and macabre but also intelligent and emotional. This breathlessly superficial show reduces it to a stylish pose Jake and Dinos Chapman were dismissed by some even in the 1990s as overgrown adolescents selling shock for its own sake, and yet it is their work that brings this dismally shallow show closest to a moment of depth. Their sculpture Great Deeds Against the Dead, based on a print of Napoleonic war atrocities by Goya, is a display of dismembered, bleeding nude corpses hung on a tree. It asks questions about war and art, the representation of pain, whether art can have a moral purpose. The best British art of the 1990s was like that, coming on as brash, vulgar, macabre, yet also unexpectedly intelligent and emotional. Unfortunately this show is neither. You’d think Tate Britain would want to do justice to a decade in which these Millbank premises played a starring role, staging the Turner prize in the years when bisected cows, concrete houses and elephant dung got the nation arguing. At the start of the 1990s no one thought Britain was a leader in contemporary art. By the millennium, we were better known for new art than new novels. Continue reading...

data.title: Burnham’s surprise EU-turn could deliver the Tories from a generational mess | Gaby Hinsliff
data.description: Badenoch would never have reopened the door on Brexit, but now that the PM has, it suits the Conservatives to let him walk through it There’s no way on earth it should have worked, but somehow he may have got away with it. Last week, the actor Richard E Grant became the first contestant on The Traitors – a show whose only unbreakable rule is never to let anyone know you’re the murderer – to gleefully announce within minutes of being selected that yes, haha, it’s him! Yet even then many of his fellow contestants seemed to like him too much to recoil. And that, roughly speaking, is now Andy Burnham’s Brexit strategy. After years of Labour politicians – not least Burnham himself, in the Makerfield byelection , without which he would not now be prime minister – trying to hide their real feelings about Brexit, Burnham has decided just to tell the truth and hope people roll with it. Leaving hasn’t worked, he said bluntly last week in Liverpool , and Britain should consider the alternatives. If you’re a leaver who suspects him of being out to unwind Brexit – well, yes, he is. This bold strategy seemingly surprised much of his own cabinet , an early lesson in how he likes to work for those who hadn’t studied his Manchester operation closely enough. But the oddly muted initial response to what would once have been a seismic shock suggests it’s wrongfooting some opponents, too. Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The butter boom – how the world fell back in love with the glorious golden spread
data.description: It’s being sculpted for fashion parties, collected by tourists and hoarded in freezers. There are even entire shops devoted to it. What’s behind the revival of the much-maligned foodstuff? Temperatures in Paris were nudging 41C when Erwan Leo opened Le Butter this summer. Wildfires had already been tearing through France and the city was quiet, particularly in the less touristy 8th arrondissement, a flex-your-wealth area near the Eiffel Tower known as the “golden triangle”. The last thing it needed, you would think, was a shop that sold loads of butter. “We were just so worried about the fridges,” says Leo, the 34-year-old owner. “We didn’t think anyone would even turn up.” I visit Le Butter, the first shop in Paris dedicated to selling the stuff, two months later in September. It’s a quaint, photogenic spot between a wine shop that was opened by Leo eight years ago and a cafe famous for being blown up in Christopher Nolan’s Inception. Inside there are candy-striped walls, little shopping baskets, a shelf of Instagrammable buttery merch (knives, hats, totes) and two double fridges containing 50 different types of butter. It’s a lot cooler today; the fridges purr away at an exacting 3C. And the past few months have been busy – so much so that Leo has had to erect a bench for those waiting outside, and a retractable barrier to manage the queues. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘They take our water, our soil’: protesters fight ‘foreignisation’ as Javier Milei encourages land sales in Argentina
data.description: The country’s far-right president is courting billionaire investors by removing a block on foreign ownership of land and natural resources On 19 September, Marta Sahores, an 84-year-old chemistry professor and activist who has mobilised against mega-mining projects for more than two decades, took to the streets in Argentina . Alongside workers, retirees, students, Indigenous groups and human rights organisations, Sahores was there to protest against the country’s far-right president, Javier Milei. During the marcha de la bronca – the “march of anger” – protesters held signs reading, among other rallying cries, “The land is not for sale”. Marching in Esquel, a town nestled in the foothills of the Andes in Chubut province, she also held up a sign defending the country’s water resources against what she called the government’s “handover” to investors. data.title: Partita By Barbara Kingsolver review – a quieter follow-up to Demon Copperhead
data.description: The sex writing threatens to throw the novel off-kilter, but there are rich rewards in this tale of music and middle-aged compromises What is the role of art in an artist’s life? Should you commit everything to honing your talent in the hope of becoming a great master? Or should you use your artistic gift to enrich your life and that of your community? In Partita, acclaimed American novelist Barbara Kingsolver grapples with these questions seriously and passionately through the story of a piano prodigy turned music teacher. The novel opens in the present, where Livia is a school music teacher in the same part of rural Tennessee where she grew up, married to a farmer who once worked on her father’s farm. Contented middle age has been disturbed by a phone call from Sigurd, a man she had an all-consuming, destructive love affair with at college. This pulls her back into her past: both the period of her brother’s suicide when she was 11, and the years when she escaped on a music scholarship to Indiana, convinced she was leaving her parents’ world behind for good. We discover that her dreams of being a world-class pianist were shattered by an accident that damaged her hand, and that Sigurd played a part in this. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I call them erotic landscapes’: fashion photographer Tim Walker on his powerful tapestry of queer Britain
data.description: He has shot everyone from Madonna to Rihanna, Kate Moss and Frank Ocean. Now Walker has turned his lens on the activists, artists, writers, models and everyday heroes of gay life Six years ago, Tim Walker was walking in the Highbury Fields area of London when he came across a plaque on the side of a building. In 1970, at these now-converted public toilets, Louis Eakes, chairman of the Young Liberals , was arrested for importuning following a “pretty police” entrapment in which male officers posed as would-be sex partners. It was here, the plaque told the photographer, that the first ever gay rights demonstration in Britain had taken place, organised by the Gay Liberation Front, in protest at Eakes’s arrest. But Walker was jolted by the date: 27 November 1970. It was the day he was born. So he wondered: “Who were those people out marching that day? Where are they now?” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘We got that bad guy and took him down!’ Jaclyn Smith on the fun, friendship and frustration of Charlie’s Angels
data.description: It’s 50 years since Smith joined TV’s bikini-clad crime fighters alongside Farrah Fawcett and Kate Jackson. She talks about the love she found on set, the harassment she endured off it and the drug-taking she did her best to ignore For a TV show that only ran for five years, Charlie’s Angels packs a punch like a bikini-wearing big-hair-flicking private investigator. “We never thought we’d be talking about it 50 years later,” says Jaclyn Smith, the only original Angel to make it to the end of the show’s run. Smith, 80, has now written a memoir, I Once Knew a Guy Called Charlie – she is not, you gather, the type of actor to want to distance herself from her defining project. As I read her book, and speak to her over Zoom, she comes across as sensible, hardworking and optimistic. Also lucky: loving and supportive parents, agents who seem to appear from nowhere and offer her work, an early hit show, a gift for making friends and getting over heartbreak. Even when she was diagnosed with breast cancer more than 20 years ago, terrifying as it was, it was caught early and successfully treated. Her positive outlook seems to extend to the excesses of US TV in the 1970s and 80s (drug use on set only gets a brief mention); her three ex-husbands get off fairly lightly; and any difficulties – her OCD, the men who stalked her at the height of her fame – are not dwelled on. Continue reading...

data.title: While British children go hungry, we waste 1.1bn meals a year. Bring on the redistribution revolution | Charlotte Hill
data.description: Food businesses and the government must make redistribution a key policy to address food insecurity. We know the surplus food is out there Charlotte Hill is chief executive of the food redistribution organisation Felix How often does this happen? You open the fridge and find some ingredient you meant to use but didn’t get round to, and even though it’s still edible you think perhaps it’s just easier to throw it away. In the UK it’s estimated that an average household wastes about three meals a week , or 156 meals a year. Household fridges are one thing. But across the food sector more than 1bn meals’ worth of easily accessible surplus food is wasted each year in the UK for the same reason: because it is easier to throw it away. That equates to 470,000 tonnes – enough to feed every child in the UK three meals a day for a month. When so many people are struggling to afford food, that is a staggering amount, and what’s even more shocking is that it is good quality and nutritious. Charlotte Hill is chief executive of the food redistribution organisation Felix Continue reading...

data.title: What have I learned in my 53 years? That I shouldn’t listen to strangers who accost me in the street | Zoe Williams
data.description: I was shocked when a man in a van aimed an ageist insult at me. And I regret to say that my son has been no help at all I was performing an ordinary and not at all illegal cycling manoeuvre recently when a guy in a white van said: “You’re too old to be that stupid.” It was a critique so devastating that I was 10 minutes down the road before I even examined its mechanics. What is the right age to make a right-hand turn? I had also previously assumed that, wearing a bike helmet, I was invisible on the road. I’d come to think of myself as a ninja or a sprite, moving like smoke through traffic, protected only by my agility and smarts. Dispiritingly, it seems I was perfectly visible and other vehicles were just choosing not to notice when I wanted to turn right. Anyway, I was on the way to meet a friend and, when I described this ageist abuse to him, he said, having quite a theatrical turn of phrase: “Darling, you’re not old enough to be this stupid.” Continue reading...

data.title: How did some City fans become aggressive defenders of a nation state’s regime? | Sean Ingle
data.description: The Manchester City case is one example of how fandom has warped beyond previous boundaries in online spaces A video of Liam Gallagher playing in a 1996 charity football match resurfaced on social media recently. Dressed in Manchester City blue and a bucket hat, in truth he appears to be in a fug of cigarettes and alcohol. But then, out of nowhere, he hits a shot into the top corner . Since last week, though, the Oasis singer has preferred to defend the honour of his club with his studs up. As the fallout from the biggest scandal in British football history headed into a second week, Gallagher was asked what he made of rival fans wanting City to lose all their trophies after being found guilty of all the serious charges against them. “There all NEUROTIC little GIMPS,” came the reply on social media. It was one of dozens of sweary, punchy, and often amusing responses, all built on a solitary article of faith: that City will somehow find a way to wriggle free. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on sexual abuse in schools: teachers cannot deal with this alone | Editorial
data.description: Politicians must redouble their efforts to tackle a disturbing pattern of pupils assaulting classmates The Guardian’s findings about the extent of sexual abuse in schools require an urgent, calibrated response. Data revealing multiple rapes committed each year on school premises in England and Wales is hard to comprehend. Yet this is what freedom of information requests to police forces, covering the period from 2021 until last year, have revealed. As well as the severity of the offences, the youth of many of the victims is disturbing. More than 8,500 sexual offences at or near schools were committed against under-13s, most of them girls. Data about perpetrators contains gaps, including their age and sex. While the overwhelming majority of such acts are carried out by boys , we don’t know the exact proportion, nor if there is an age gap between those carrying out abuse and those being targeted. Only 33 out of 43 police forces shared their data, meaning that large areas including Scotland are not represented. But whatever the exact details, and allowing for the fact that these are reports, not convictions, the findings are deeply dismaying. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...

data.title: The Breakdown | From France to Old Reigatians: the most inspiring sides in rugby history
data.description: The most memorable teams aren’t always the the most famous – and the key ingredients have remained the same for many years It is an entirely subjective question but still worth pondering as the autumn mists descend. What is the most inspiring rugby team you ever saw? Not the absolute best, necessarily, because that is too restrictive a filter. This is about sides who, in addition to stringing a few wins together, had something about them that still captures the imagination even decades later. In part these things are shaped by timing and circumstance. You never forget the first international you attended, say, or how that experience made you feel. For anyone who has stood in the Shed for years, the sight of Gloucester sitting atop the English Prem table may just be stirring similar emotions. That said, it may still take a while for this year’s squad to nudge past Teague, Fidler and Blakeway in the Cherry & White hall of fame. Continue reading...

data.title: Schooled for success: how English lessons power Midtjylland’s talent factory
data.description: In a squad with 17 nationalities from five continents, communication is key – and the Danish club enjoyed a bumper summer transfer window If there is a secret to Midtjylland’s success in the transfer market then it starts in the classroom. Before this summer the Danish club renowned for an innovative approach had banked more than €200m (£170m) in sales since 2018, and they have just enjoyed the most profitable window in their short history. The departure of the Guinea-Bissau striker Franculino Djú for Trabzonspor and the Chile forward Darío Osorio’s move to Crystal Palace on loan with an obligation to buy will potentially bring in €62m (£53.2m), with both deals completed in 48 hours at the end of the window. That followed the departures of the homegrown winger Aral Simsir and South Korean defender Lee Han-beom for Club Brugge for another €25m. The next batch of recruits included David Martínez, a 20-year-old Venezuela international from the MLS side LAFC. “I think hectic will be a good word,” says the technical director, Kristian Kjær, of the past couple of months. Continue reading...

data.title: Saints’ lopsided loss sours celebrations on 20th anniversary of ‘Domecoming’
data.description: Falcons ease to 45-24 win and silence Superdome crowd Match marked two decades since return post-Katrina The New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough was “embarrassed”. The second-year coach Kellen Moore was “disappointed” and “frustrated”. And a day of festivities commemorating one of the most triumphant moments in the New Orleans Saints’ history ended with boos and early exits. Three plays into Monday night’s game against Atlanta, the Falcons running back Bijan Robinson silenced an electric Superdome crowd with a 59-yard touchdown run. The Saints’ performance in a 45-24 loss to the Falcons bore no resemblance to their landmark 23-3 victory against the same team 20 years ago , when the venue finally reopened after being damaged by Hurricane Katrina. On that made-for-TV night, Steve Gleason blocked a punt on the Falcons’ opening possession and Curtis Deloatch recovered it for a touchdown, sending the Saints on their way. Continue reading...

data.title: Nations League roundup: Olise leads late charge as France bowl over Belgium
data.description: France score four goals in 14 minutes to triumph Italy see off Turkey, Hungary edge out Ukraine Michael Olise came off the bench to inspire France to a 4-1 win over Belgium in the Nations League, handing Zinedine Zidane his first home victory since taking charge. Dodi Lukébakio put Belgium on course for their first competitive win over Les Bleus in 45 years when he fired the visitors in front in the first half at the Stade de France. But the hosts turned the match on its head in a blistering finish, scoring four times in 14 minutes to preserve Zidane’s unbeaten start and move closer to the quarter-finals. Continue reading...

data.title: Ronaldo’s break with Portugal is sad, fitting, and long overdue | Jonathan Wilson
data.description: The star’s rift with Jorge Jesus is an unfortunate affair. But the forward has been holding his national team back for years Sign up for our free newsletter here If this is to be the end for Cristiano Ronaldo at international level, at least it can be said that he left the stage as he bestrode it: with monumental self-regard. Ronaldo has always been a preening, self-absorbed player, but for a time, when he was one of the best in the world, it could be tolerated. For the past four years, though, he has actively and obviously held Portugal back. There is a great generation of technical talent here weighed down by the monstrous albatross of his ego. To recap the basic details of the past couple of weeks. Ronaldo played 67 minutes of Portugal’s scratchy 1-0 win over Wales . Portugal coach Jorge Jesus, who replaced Roberto Martínez after the World Cup, said he had a verbal agreement with Ronaldo that he would not start the following game against Norway but would perhaps come off the bench. Early in the second half, Ronaldo went to warm up – although whether that was on his own initiative or because Jesus had told him to is unclear. The game was tight, Portugal ultimately winning 2-1, and Jesus did not bring Ronaldo on. Continue reading...

data.title: Celibidache was a musical visionary, an uncompromising perfectionist – and my father
data.description: The legendary conductor was acclaimed for his dazzling music-making, and infamous for his hatred of recordings. His son, writer of a new film about him, remembers a loving yet intransigent and demanding father My father, Sergiu Celibidache, loved children more than anything because they are free and true to themselves. And yet, he once made a young boy wet himself when he dared to ask for an autograph, shouting at the poor child as if he had committed a federal crime because he knew there was a black market selling his signature behind his back. I grew up a privileged child with presents from all around the world. I was spoiled – to the despair of my mother, who always tried to keep my feet on the ground. But the gifts were part of my father’s way of making up for his long absences – he was often away touring with his orchestras. Continue reading...

data.title: Comédie Française review – pre-show bedlam plays theatrical chaos for laughs
data.description: French farce set in the tumultuous three hours prior to the opening night performance of Macbeth features comic-timing perfection from cast One of Matt Groening’s Life In Hell comic strips from the 1980s, entitled How to Be a Clever Film Critic , sets out cinema’s greatest paradox: “The French are funny. Sex is funny. And comedies are funny. Yet no French sex comedies are funny.” Well, this film from Bertrand Usclat and Martin Darondeau proves that all commonly held certitudes must be disproved at some point, because here’s a French comedy, albeit one that’s not all that preoccupied with sex, that is a hoot. Set entirely in the Parisian institution of the title , this frothy farce unfolds over the three hours before the opening night curtain goes up on a production of Macbeth, which is being directed by actor turned metteur en scène Nina (Pauline Clément). A series of catastrophes make it an open question as to whether the show will actually go on, starting from the moment Nina arrives at the entrance without her staff pass and has to try to get past the officious security team. Naturally, that’s just the beginning, and Nina must contend with superstitious actors, adulterous actors shagging while they rehearse (saying their lines between thrusts), a stoned grande dame (Danièle Lebrun), missing actors (Lady Macbeth is stranded in Brest while shooting a TV show on the side) and actors who understand their roles less than the usher (Sefa Yeboah), who is watching from the sidelines. data.title: The Lost Children of Tuam review – deeply serious retelling of Ireland’s devastating tragedy
data.description: Monica Dolan is superb as the amateur historian who uncovered the horror of mass graves at a mother and baby home in this Liam Neeson produced drama The children were never lost; if a baby goes missing, the police get called, social services become involved. The babies born at the mother and baby home run by nuns in the town of Tuam in County Galway were discarded: up to 796 tiny bodies thrown away, some in an old sewage tank. The amateur historian who uncovered the horror of the mass graves at the St Mary’s mother and baby home is Catherine Corless, superbly played here by Monica Dolan. Produced by Liam Neeson, and based on a 2017 New York Times article , The Lost Children of Tuam is a painful, devastating film. It feels scraped clean of anything unnecessary that might trivialise, fiction-ise or movie-ise what happened at St Mary’s, home to thousands of unmarried women and children between 1925 and 1961. “It gets me out of the house,” Corless says when she starts a course in local history. She turns detective after becoming interested in the children from St Mary’s, and what she uncovers is that babies died at a rate of nearly one a fortnight at the home – from whooping cough, measles, malnutrition and other childhood illnesses. Eventually, she obtains nearly 800 death certificates, but cannot find burial records for the babies. There are no graves. Continue reading...

data.title: The Craft review – cult high-school horror a reminder of the fearless 90s
data.description: The 30th-anniversary rerelease of this classic tackles the sensitivities of teenage anxiety with energy and confidence The chrysalis of 80s and 90s high-school comedy finally gave us a veritable butterfly of fear in this cult girl-power classic from 1996, co-written and directed by Andrew Fleming, now rereleased for its 30th anniversary. It’s a movie to compare with Heathers or Mean Girls but with a supernatural edge, a flourish of scariness where the comedy or sexiness might otherwise go – and it incidentally delivers a very disturbing “René Magritte mirror” visual stab worthy of any straight-ahead chiller. Robin Tunney plays Sarah, a shy, studious teen from San Francisco who suffers from depression and buried guilt about the fact that her mother died in childbirth, and from lingering resentment at her new stepmother, with whom her dad has bought her to Los Angeles for a fresh start at a new school. Something about this new arrival intrigues a clique nicknamed “the bitches of Eastwick”, led by badass goth Nancy (Fairuza Balk); she rules over her two disciples Rochelle (Rachel True) and Bonnie, played by Neve Campbell, that same year to become a scary-movie hall-of-famer for the fledgling Scream franchise. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Exceptionally crafted’: why Little Shop of Horrors is my feelgood movie
data.description: The latest in our series of writers’ favorite comfort films is a tribute to the lovably quirky 80s musical The key to a feelgood movie , beyond the necessary rewatchability, is familiarity – the real kind that lets you look away or fall asleep without doubting your affection. Musicals are perfectly suited to this particular subgenre since the majority of them, especially the classic ones adapted for film, atrophy with second-act problems. That’s where writers suddenly remember the plot they had introduced and drop all that singing and dancing to arrive at some type of conclusion. The first act of Funny Girl? A near-flawless parade of showstoppers, Barbra Streisand as Fanny Brice having the time of her life falling in love. I’ve probably seen it 200 times. The second act … well, who ever cared about her husband’s gambling addiction? Continue reading...

data.title: Holding Lightning by Emily Lordi review – an intimate portrait of Whitney Houston
data.description: An empathetic biography of the the singer recasts her tumultuous later career as a triumph of self-expression Since Whitney Houston’s death in 2012, a flurry of books and documentaries have appeared, most of them presenting her life as a cautionary tale. In this new biography, Emily Lordi, a professor of English at Vanderbilt University, refuses to reduce Houston’s story to another “good girl gone bad” narrative. Instead she presents a pluralistic take on her life in which Houston’s queerness, drug use and eccentricities are not dismissed as aberrations (as they were in her lifetime) but rather seen in the wider context of her unique talent and the pressures placed on her to embody black excellence. Lordi describes the unsteady building blocks of Houston’s family (her mother Cissy’s band The Sweet Inspirations were in-demand session musicians who worked with Elvis, as well as on Van Morrison’s Brown Eyed Girl and Dusty Springfield’s Son of a Preacher Man). When Cissy was still a child, Houston’s grandmother had a debilitating stroke following a miscarriage, eventually succumbing to a cerebral haemorrhage during a later pregnancy. The response to this trauma was to bury it. As Lordi writes: “Here was a lesson in suppressing your feelings and getting on with it.” But in a book where the act of singing through the pain is invoked multiple times, it is striking that reports Houston was molested as a child (a pivotal part of Kevin Macdonald’s 2018 documentary, which drew a line between that and her addictions) are not discussed. Continue reading...

It is also the murder weapon in the killing of Scatman Crothers’ character, Dick Hallorann. One of cinema’s most famous axes could be yours for a list price of between £30,000 and £50,000. data.title: Post your questions for Sofia Coppola
data.description: A new documentary by Eleanor Coppola goes behind the scenes on her daughter’s 2006 punk classic, Marie Antoinette. To mark its release, Sofia Coppola will be taking your questions To say that Sofia Coppola grew up on screen would be an understatement. The youngest child and only daughter of filmmaker Francis Ford Coppola and documentary-maker Eleanor Coppola, she appeared in all three Godfather films: as the baby being christened in 1972’s The Godfather, as a child on the steamboat in 1974’s The Godfather Part II, and, aged 19, as Mary Corleone in 1990’s The Godfather Part III. In between came small roles in several of her dad’s films, including 1983’s The Outsiders and Rumble Fish, 1984’s The Cotton Club and 1986’s Peggy Sue Got Married, in which she played Kathleen Turner’s younger sister Nancy. She also popped up all over 1990s music videos, playing a wild-eyed Joan Crawford in Sonic Youth’s 1990 Mildred Pierce, a troubled drifter in the Black Crowes’ 1992 Sometimes Salvation, one of Madonna’s clubbing friends in 1992’s Deeper and Deeper, and an injured gymnast in the Chemical Brothers’ 1997 Elektrobank, directed by her then-boyfriend Spike Jonze. Continue reading...

data.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the cockroaches I still dream about
data.description: My student house in Manchester had several thousand other occupants. Despite pest controllers regularly dousing the property, the glossy, greasy, relentless insects marched onwards, endlessly reproducing ‘You do know about the cockroaches?” I’ve forgotten most things people said to me in the 80s, but never that. It was said by one of the occupants of the student house in Longsight, Manchester, that I had signed up to live in the following year. When the landlord had shown me and my future housemates the property, the tenants had been out. He told us they were third years doing their finals and must not be disturbed under any circumstances. (What can I say? We were gullible back then.) Days before summer term ended though, I’d knocked on the door to show a friend where I’d be living. Instead, I learned that the house was infested. The weird thing is, we moved in anyway. In truth, although I understood this was very bad news, I didn’t quite realise what a cockroach was. There was no internet, so I would have had to go to a library to know what I know now: their march, their canter, their crunch if you step on one. Their soft, sweet, sour smell (uric acid which they store in their fat, apparently). Sometimes, in the back of a shop, or a restaurant loo, I catch that scent and I know what it is. Continue reading...

data.title: Jose Pizarro’s recipe for poached pear and almond tart with PX caramel
data.description: This tart uses the richness of red vermut to bring together the sweet and the nutty for a flavour explosion In Spain, vermut is traditionally enjoyed as an aperitif, while pedro ximénez is often poured at the end of a meal, alongside dessert or a piece of cheese, say. In this tart, however, they come together to tell the story of the Spanish table in the form of pudding. We have a wonderful tradition of fortified wines, and while lighter sherries often hog the limelight, vermut and pedro ximénez deserve just as much attention. They’re both made from wine, but each brings something completely different to a dish. Here, vermut, which is infused with herbs and spices, gently perfumes the pears, while PX, with its rich raisin, fig and caramel notes, introduces a flavour that’s impossible to resist. data.title: Chanel is all about joy as Blazy celebrates year at helm of world’s hottest brand
data.description: Artistic director is all smiles as he swaps quiet luxury for bold colours and patterns at Paris show “It’s a good start,” Matthieu Blazy said after a Paris show that marked a year of his tenure as artistic director at Chanel. “I am happy with where we are at.” Chanel now holds the top spot in the Lyst index of the world’s hottest brands, which tracks demand and engagement across search and social media. The privately held company announces official financial results only once a year, but figures reported by Bloomberg showed 16% growth in the first half of 2026. In Vanity Fair’s list of the world’s 50 most powerful people, published this month, Blazy is the only fashion designer to make the cut. data.title: Houseplant hacks: Are windowsills too cold for plants in winter?
data.description: It may be flooded with light, but that window ledge is only a pane of glass away from the elements. What’s the best way to protect your plants? The problem That bright window spot you chose for your houseplants to receive maximum sunlight can become one of the coldest places in the house in winter. The glass itself can get cold, and with heavy curtains drawn, it creates a cooler box area around your window. For tropical plants like anthuriums and philodendrons, which are used to less temperature fluctuation, the cold can be fatal. The hack Move sensitive plants back from the glass overnight, then return them to their brighter position in the morning. Continue reading...

data.title: Country diary: On the bluest of days, the plaintive call of a pipit | Mark Cocker
data.description: Combs Moss, Derbyshire: There is plenty to be gloomy about, but today was not the day for it up on the moor The morning was sunlit and the sky the sort of deepest blue dome that makes your heart sing – and all the louder for being at the time of least natural sound. Autumn is the most silent season for birds, but at least I could hear the passing meadow pipits more clearly as they came out of the blue in small numbers and crossed overhead on migration. There is something inherently melancholic about their plaintive piping calls , which seem at one with the mood of upland treeless places. Continue reading...

data.title: Ageing mice study finds why 'zombie cells' evade immune clearance and fuel inflammation
data.description: Researchers studying ageing in mice have found that a decline in chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA), a cellular recycling process, helps “zombie cells” accumulate by weakening the immune system’s ability to clear them. Restoring CMA reduced senescent-cell buildup, inflammation and fibrosis in mice, pointing to a possible new approach to age-related diseases.

data.title: La moitié des aidants ayant besoin de répit peinent à l’obtenir : « J’étais trop épuisée pour prendre le temps de chercher »
data.description: Seules 49 % des personnes qui aident un proche au quotidien et expriment le besoin de faire une pause l’obtiennent, selon une étude publiée à l’occasion de la Journée nationale des aidants du 6 octobre. Les freins peuvent être administratifs, financiers, mais aussi liés à la définition même de l’aidant.

data.title: Cúpula discute integração do ensino superior entre Europa e América Latina
data.description: Um estudante brasileiro termina a graduação na Europa e, de volta ao Brasil, enfrenta dificuldades para validar as disciplinas cursadas ou reconhecer o diploma obtido no exterior. Os empecilhos aumentam quando diferentes países têm regras próprias para validar disciplinas e formações. data.title: Atak dronów u wybrzeży Bułgarii. Jeden statek zatonął, los załogi nieznany
data.description: Premier bułgarskiego rządu Rumen Radew potwierdził doniesienia prasy, że drony morskie i powietrzne zaatakowały dwa statki handlowe w Wyłącznej Strefie Ekonomicznej Bułgarii na Morzu Czarnym. Nie sprecyzował, czy były to drony rosyjskie, czy ukraińskie. Jeden ze statków zatonął  i dotąd nie odnaleziono członków jego załogi. Na drugim statku wybuchł pożar, a załogę pomyślnie ewakuowano.

data.title: Už nejde jen o školy. Francie se otřásá, vláda hájí nasazení policejních granátů
data.description: Ve Francii začal další den blokád škol a demonstrací, do nichž se v mnoha městech zapojí také odbory. V Paříži je očekáváno až 40 tisíc účastníků protestního průvodu. Kromě toho jsou plánované demonstrace v dalších velkých městech. Demonstranti a odborové organizace požadují, aby vláda řešila situaci, kdy školy trpí nedostatkem personálu a jsou údajně ve zchátralém stavu.

data.title: Kroměříž hledá novou tvář Velkého náměstí, rozhodnou budoucí zastupitelé
data.description: Velké náměstí, které je pomyslným srdcem Kroměříže, má být po své proměně příjemnějším místem pro lidi. Na tom se místní politici shodují. Část z nich připouští výraznější omezení parkování a postupné vytlačení aut z historického centra, jiní zase varují před příliš rychlým úbytkem míst pro řidiče. Všichni ale chtějí více zeleně, restauračních zahrádek či lepší podmínky pro pěší. O podobě hlavního náměstí ovšem rozhodnou až budoucí zastupitelé.

data.title: Opatření při suchu. Co všechno mohou úřady zakázat, když dojde voda
data.description: Překročení Lipna suchou nohou, hladina Orlíku na historickém minimu nebo vyschlá koryta řek. V takových extrémních situacích se do boje proti nedostatku vody v krajině mohou vložit obce i stát – na řadu pak přicházejí nejrůznější zákazy a omezení, jejichž cílem je srazit spotřebu na minimum a zároveň co nejvíce vláhy udržet v krajině.

data.title: Zeman kritizoval kolaboraci. Vytkl Pavlovi záštitu Sudetoněmeckému dni v Brně
data.description: Do prezidenta Petra Pavla se pustil jeho předchůdce Miloš Zeman. Vyčetl mu záštitu, kterou udělil festivalu Meeting Brno, jehož zástupci pozvali do Brna v květnu sjezd Sudetoněmeckého krajanského sdružení. „Kolaborace se rodí ze zbabělosti a vrcholí zradou vlastního národa,“ řekl ve Sněmovně Zeman.

data.title: Nové sportovní haly i knihovny. Politici doručují mnoho slibů těsně před volbami
data.description: Kromě předvolebních slibů se na podzim nápadně objevuje i množství hotových projektů. Politici přestřihávají pásky u sportovišť a knihoven, opravují školy i veřejná prostranství. data.title: Milenci zasadila 158 ran nožem. Zacpávala jsem mu pusu a omlouvala se, líčila u soudu
data.description: Po setkání v parku se přisunuli na ubytovnu, kde pili alkohol a měli intimní styk. Při něm vzala Lucie Hrdová do ruky kuchyňský nůž a muži zasadila 158 bodných a řezných ran. O pár měsíců dřív jiného muže shodila z mostu a zbila. Pokusem o vraždu a vraždou s rozmyslem spáchanou zvlášť surovým způsobem v Jevišovicích na Znojemsku se dnes začal zabývat Krajský soud v Brně. Ženě hrozí 15 až 20 let vězení, případně výjimečný trest - doživotí.

data.title: Drony zasáhly dvě lodi v ekonomické zóně Bulharska, jedna z nich se potopila
data.description: Drony zasáhly dvě lodi v ekonomické zóně Bulharska, uvedl v úterý premiér země Rumen Radev. Podle něj se jedno plavidlo potopilo a posádka je nezvěstná. Druhou loď zachvátil požár, námořníky se ale podařilo evakuovat. Bulharská média píší o bezprecedentním koordinovaném útoku na obchodní plavidla v Černém moři.

data.title: Slabý článek sankčního řetězu. Jižní Korea dodává palivo Rusku, zjistila analýza
data.description: Moskva se uprostřed války s Ukrajinou zoufale snaží zajistit si dostatečné zásoby paliva. V červenci a srpnu letošního roku do ruských přístavů doputovalo více než 150 000 tun paliva z Jižní Koreje. Stalo se tak zčásti za pomoci tankerů, na které se vztahují sankce. Tento krok je v rozporu s veřejnou podporou Kyjevu, kterou se Soul ohání, zjistila analýza britského deníku.

data.title: Oslnilo mě slunce, hájil se mladý řidič porsche. V protisměru smetl cyklistu
data.description: Do Fakultní nemocnice Olomouc byl v pondělí letecky transportován cyklista, který byl účastníkem dopravní nehody. Při průjezdu zatáčkou do něj narazilo Porsche, jež šoféroval mladý řidič. „Po nárazu byl cyklista odhozen do příkopu a došlo k jeho zranění,“ informovala v úterý policejní mluvčí Miluše Zajícová.

data.title: Nástup „Jihlaváka“, úprk komunistů, TOP 09 bez značky. A Brod má volební rekord
data.description: Hned dvanáct uskupení vstoupí v Havlíčkově Brodě do komunálních voleb. Nikdy v historii jich tolik nebylo, je to rekord. Posty obhajuje velká většina zastupitelů, jen výjimečně se na špičkách kandidátek objevují nová jména. Některá ovšem stojí za pozornost. Starostou by se rád znovu stal Zbyněk Stejskal z ODS.

data.title: Dálnice D35 bude rozestavěná celá. Stát vybral zhotovitele největší PPP zakázky
data.description: Do samotného finále vstoupil největší dálniční PPP projekt v Česku. Ministerstvo dopravy vybralo konsorcium, které během následujících šesti let postaví 35,4 kilometru dlouhou dálnici D35 mezi Svitavami a Mohelnicí. „Naším cílem je stavbu rozjet nejpozději na přelomu roku,“ uvedl ministr dopravy Ivan Bednárik.

data.title: Vakcínu na covid dál nebude kupovat stát, úhradu posoudí SÚKL, řekl Vojtěch
data.description: Vakcínu proti covidu-19 nebude od roku 2027 dál zajišťovat stát, řekl ministr zdravotnictví Adam Vojtěch (ANO). Státní ústav pro kontrolu léčiv (SÚKL) posoudí její přínos a stanoví případnou úhradu z veřejného zdravotního pojištění nebo výši doplatku, doplnil zástupce hlavního hygienika Matyáš Fošum.

data.title: Tlakoměr za méně než devět set korun v redakčním testu. Co umí SimplyMed C02?
data.description: Pažní tlakoměr SimplyMed C02 patří k cenově dostupným přístrojům pro domácí kontrolu tlaku. V redakčním testu jsme prověřili jeho ovládání, komfort při měření i přehlednost displeje. Zajímalo nás, zda dokáže v běžném provozu nabídnout spolehlivé a jednoduché řešení pro celou rodinu.

data.title: OBRAZEM: Slapy vysychají před očima. Voda odkryla dno, lodě i tisíce škeblí
data.description: Hladina Slapské přehrady kvůli extrémnímu hydrologickému suchu v minulých dnech dál klesala a dostala se už pod úroveň běžnou pro zimní období. Ustupující voda odkryla rozsáhlé části břehů i dna, komplikuje provoz lodí a na některých místech zanechala na suchu tisíce škeblí. Povodí Vltavy přitom vodu ze Slap využívá k udržení potřebného průtoku Vltavy.

data.title: Může se Pavel vrátit na volby? Je to na rozhodnutí prezidenta, uvedl mluvčí
data.description: I když dal prezident Petr Pavel přednost soukromé zahraniční cestě před účastí u komunálních voleb, varianta, že se po vlně kritiky ještě na volby přece jen vrátí, nemusí být vyloučena. Alespoň podle vyjádření ředitele tiskového odboru Hradu Víta Koláře. „Je to na rozhodnutí prezidenta. Nevolám mu. Prezident zvažoval a přemýšlel o tom, co to může přinést,“ sdělil iDNES.cz Kolář.

data.title: Dostupné bydlení má zajistit město, míní Erbsová. Cílí na komunitu a mladé rodiny
data.description: Uskupení Změna a Zelení dokázalo hradecké zastupitelstvo pořádně provětrat už několikrát. Letos se navíc v boji o hradeckou radnici spojilo i s lidovci a nová volební jednička by mohla přinést ještě silnější vítr. Šéfka Centra uměleckých aktivit Martina Erbsová si dokáže představit spolupráci na formátu současné koalice. Zároveň odmítá, že by byla melounem, zeleným navenek a rudým uvnitř.

data.title: Scio chce založit vysokou školu. Slibuje tisíce hodin praxe i inspiraci Finskem
data.description: Nová soukromá vysoká škola nevznikla v Česku už deset let. Společnost Scio chce nyní jednu založit v Praze, fungovat by mohla už od září 2027. Čeká však ještě na schválení. Postavená by měla být především na praxi. „Přijde nám, že vysoké školství je strašně konzervativní. Studenti sedí v posluchárnách a z naprosté většiny je to o pasivním příjmu informací,“ říká spolumajitel Scia Jan Šotola.

data.title: Radní Pražských služeb si stěžují na šikanu, zastrašování a politický nátlak
data.description: Krátce před komunálními volbami se v metropoli znovu vyostřuje dlouholetý spor o kontrolu městské společnosti Pražské služby, která zajišťuje svoz odpadu v Praze. Sedm z dvanácti členů dozorčí rady zaslalo vedení magistrátu otevřený dopis, ve kterém si stěžují na zastrašování, urážky i politický nátlak. Hlavním terčem kritiky je předseda rady Lukáš Wagenknecht, nominovaný Piráty. Ten však jakákoli obvinění odmítá a tvrdí, že jde o účelovou předvolební kampaň.

data.title: I jedenáct lidí do jednoho bytu. Špindlerovu Mlýnu před volbami přibývá obyvatelstvo
data.description: Radnice ve Špindlerově Mlýně prověřuje náhlý nárůst trvale bydlících obyvatel. Těsně před volbami se do jediného bytu přihlásilo 11 osob, od začátku roku jde už o 40 nových voličů. Starosta krkonošského střediska Martin Jandura (Špindlerův Mlýn - Město s vizí) to považuje za snahu ovlivnit volby a ovládnout radnici. Podnikl proti tomu právní kroky.

data.title: UAE and Jordan begin construction of railway to transport phosphate to Red Sea port
data.description: Jordan and the UAE have begun constructing the Aqaba–Shidiya–Maan railway, a major transport project overseen by King Abdullah and Abu Dhabi crown prince Sheikh Khaled. The railway, managed by the UAE–Jordan Railway Company, will transport approximately 13 million tonnes of phosphate annually from Shidiya mines to the Red Sea port of Aqaba. This initiative aims to enhance phosphate transport, reduce shipping costs, and connect Jordan's resources to international markets.

data.title: US envoy holds rare meeting with Sudan’s top general in push to seek end to fighting
data.description: A US envoy recently held a rare meeting with Sudan's top general, Abdel-Fattah Burhan, in a push by the Trump administration to end the country's devastating conflict. This diplomatic effort, hosted by Egyptian President El-Sisi, aims to restore Sudan's stability, facilitate reconstruction, and transition toward a civilian-led government. The war has created the world's largest humanitarian crisis, displacing millions and causing widespread famine, prompting the US and other intermediaries to renew pressure for negotiations and a humanitarian truce.

data.title: Telerrobótica, clave en la lucha contra el tiempo para tratar un accidente cerebrovascular
data.description: Durante un accidente cerebrovascular isquémico, el cerebro puede perder cerca de dos millones de neuronas por minuto, por lo que el tiempo en que se recibe un tratamiento es clave para disminuir el riesgo de muerte y secuelas; por esto, la empresa XCath realizó este año en Panamá, con su sistema Iris, la primera trombectomía mecánica telerrobótica a distancia en un paciente con ictus.

data.title: Linafoot : le championnat national démarre le 20 octobre avec plusieurs matchs au programme
data.description: La Ligue nationale de football (Linafoot) a dévoilé, lundi 5 octobre 2026, le calendrier général de la 32ᵉ édition du championnat national, Ligue 1, pour la saison 2026-2027. Le coup d’envoi est fixé au mardi 20 octobre, avec cinq rencontres prévues lors de la première journée dans les groupes A et B. Lupopo, Mazembe et les autres affiches du groupe A Dans le groupe A, le FC Saint-Eloi Lupopo recevra l’AS New Soger. Le CS Don Bosco sera opposé à l’AS Malole, tandis que l’AS Simba accueillera l’AS Saint-Luc.

data.title: 50 pêcheurs sensibilisés à la prévention de la maladie du sommeil à Bandundu
data.description: Cinquante pêcheurs ont été sensibilisés lundi 5 octobre à Bandundu, dans la province du Kwilu, sur les moyens de prévenir, dépister et prendre en charge la maladie du sommeil. L’activité a été menée par le Programme national de lutte contre la trypanosomiase humaine africaine dans le Kwilu. Une attention particulière a été accordée à ces professionnels régulièrement présents dans les zones de pêche et le long des cours d’eau.

data.title: La société civile de Basoko dénonce l’impact de l’exploitation de l’or sur la rivière Aruwimi
data.description: La société civile du territoire de Basoko, dans la province de Tshopo, tire la sonnette d’alarme sur les conséquences environnementales et socioéconomiques de l’exploitation aurifère dans la rivière Aruwimi. Elle accuse certaines entreprises minières opérant dans la région d’utiliser des dragues et des robots pour extraire l’or du lit de la rivière, une pratique qui, selon elle, dégrade la qualité de l’eau et menace la biodiversité locale.

data.title: OSP to rely on bank, mobile money records in Mustapha Hamid case
data.description:
The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) is set to rely on bank and mobile money accounts, associated transactions and hundreds of documents in its criminal case against former National Petroleum Authority (NPA) Chief Executive, Mustapha Hamid, and other accused persons.

The case involves officials of the NPA and several associated companies who are facing charges including alleged large-scale extortion, abuse of public office and money laundering.

According to the charge sheet being prosecuted by the OSP, the alleged offences involve sums totalling approximately GH¢291 million and more than US$300,000.

data.title: PURC replaces 10 damaged transformers affecting over 60,000 customers in Central Region
data.description:
The Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC) has facilitated the replacement of 10 damaged and overloaded electricity distribution transformers across the Central Region following persistent complaints about prolonged power outages.

The intervention, undertaken through the Commission’s Central Regional Office in collaboration with the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG), is expected to improve electricity supply to approximately 61,004 customers in the affected communities.

Some residents and businesses had endured outages for weeks, with consumers in some communities reportedly going without electricity for nearly two months.

The affected communities include Ajumako-Bisease, Katakyiase, Saltpond-Kurankyekrom, Cape Coast-Social Welfare, Nyankumasi Ahenkro, Saltpond Town, Agona, Anomabo, Ekumfi Edukuma and Gomoamaim.

data.title: NAIMOS finds illegal miners replacing destroyed Changfan machines along Pra River
data.description:
The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has intensified its crackdown on illegal mining along the Pra River, with a second sweep uncovering attempts by miners to replace equipment destroyed during an earlier operation.

The latest operation targeted illegal mining sites at Tweapease and Adiemra as part of efforts to sustain the gains made during the initial raid.

At Adiemra, the team discovered that some illegal miners had already brought in new Changfan machines to replace equipment burnt by NAIMOS personnel the previous day.

The soldiers retrieved one of the newly installed Changfan machines hidden in the bush, while other equipment mounted on rafts was set ablaze.

data.title: Deaths of three children in Tamale vehicle now being treated as murder – Police
data.description:
Police in the Northern Region are treating the deaths of three children found in the trunk of a vehicle as a murder case after a preliminary autopsy indicated that they did not die of natural causes.

The children — Dauda Abdul Aziz, 3, Saani Alsharaf, 5, and Dauda Fadilan, 7 — were found dead in the boot of a black Hyundai Tucson at Koblimahagu Zoo in the Tamale Metropolis on Monday morning.

The children had reportedly left home on Sunday to attend Islamic classes but failed to return.

According to JoyNews sources, preliminary findings from the autopsy indicate that the children may have been murdered.

data.title: Health experts warn women against unregulated breast enlargement products, herbal remedies
data.description:
Health experts have cautioned women against relying on unregulated breast enlargement products and herbal remedies to address breast-related concerns, warning that some may contain harmful substances or delay the diagnosis of serious conditions.

The warning was issued during a breast cancer awareness programme organised by the Ministry of Roads and Highways in Accra.

A midwife at the Ridge Hospital, Abigail Asiamah, said some women delay seeking medical attention when they notice changes in their breasts because they turn to herbal preparations or other unverified treatments.

She warned that such practices could make it more difficult for health professionals to diagnose and treat conditions at an early stage.

data.title: Vice President hopeful of swift end to teacher strike
data.description:
Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has expressed optimism that the ongoing strike by teacher unions will be resolved soon, saying negotiations between government and the unions have reached an advanced stage.

Speaking at the 2026 Ghana Teacher Prize ceremony in Accra, she said she was encouraged by the progress made in the discussions and expressed hope that the engagements would bring an end to the impasse.

“I’m, however, encouraged by the progress made so far. Talks between government and the unions are well advanced and I am hopeful that the constructive engagements we have seen will lead us to a resolution very soon,” she said.

The Vice President also highlighted the critical role teachers play in the country’s education system, describing teaching as “one of our most important professions.”

data.title: ‘Is 24-hour Market concept still part of 24-hour Economy?’ – Hassan Ayariga asks government
data.description:
The Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Hassan Ayariga, has called on the government to clarify its policy direction following the apparent change in terminology from “24-hour Markets” to “District Model Markets.”

In a statement issued on Monday, October 5, Ayariga said the 24-hour Market concept had become closely associated with the government’s flagship 24-hour Economy policy and had given the programme a visible and practical identity.

He said the concept created an understanding that selected markets and commercial centres could operate beyond conventional working hours, creating opportunities for businesses, traders, workers and consumers.

Hassan Ayariga said any decision to change the name or identity of the initiative must be properly explained to the public.

data.title: Barbados: Memoria que arde y resiste
data.description: Era 6 de octubre de 1976 y un avión de Cubana de Aviación despegó de Barbados para quedar, minutos después, partido en dos por la explosión de dos bombas C-4. No hubo sobrevivientes. Barbados es la cara más visible, la más evidente, de una política de terrorismo de Estado que ha probado casi todas sus armas contra Cuba, por el grave delito de no saber ser sumiso ante el Imperio: invasión, sabotaje, bandidismo, magnicidio, guerra sucia, terrorismo. The post Barbados: Memoria que arde y resiste first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.description: José Francisco Molina compareció en conferencia de prensa luego del empate 1-1 de Honduras ante Jamaica , resultado que permitió a la Selección Nacional evitar el descenso a la Liga B y mantenerse en la A de la Concacaf Nations League 2026-27 . El entrenador español analizó el desarrollo del partido y explicó cómo el gol recibido condicionó al equipo durante varios minutos: "Yo creo que al principio empezamos bien. El equipo empezó dominando el balón, teniendo un buen posicionamiento... Es verdad que luego perdimos el control del partido. Encajamos un gol prácticamente en la primera vez que chutaron. Y eso nos generó demasiada incertidumbre". Molina explicó que durante el descanso buscó recuperar la tranquilidad y corregir el posicionamiento del equipo para que Honduras volviera a tomar el control del encuentro: "En el descanso lo que ajustamos fue, sobre todo, esa tranquilidad y ese posicionamiento que necesitábamos para dominar de verdad el partido y poder hacerle daño a Jamaica. Estoy muy contento por el trabajo, por el esfuerzo del equipo... Lógicamente no estoy contento con el resultado, me hubiese gustado ganar con la diferencia de goles necesaria". Uno de los temas consultados al técnico fue la decisión de utilizar a Clinton Bennet como lateral derecho. José Molina defendió la elección y explicó que tomó en cuenta el desgaste de Cristopher Meléndez , quien había disputado tres partidos consecutivos: "Entendí que hoy era la mejor opción después de haber jugado Meléndez tres partidos seguidos. Una de las razones que me hace inclinarme por Clinton Bennet es porque creo que nos puede servir en esas dos posiciones. Estoy contento del trabajo que hizo Clinton, creo que nos ayudó". También fue consultado por la situación de David Ruiz , quien no tuvo minutos durante esta larga Fecha FIFA . El entrenador destacó las condiciones del joven futbolista y aseguró que tendrá importancia en el futuro de la Selección de Honduras : "David Ruiz es un jugador que me encanta y que por diferentes situaciones de momentos de juego y de lo que yo entendía que el partido necesitaba, al final desgraciadamente se ha quedado sin jugar un minuto. Es un jugador joven y estoy seguro de que será un jugador importante en la 'H' en algún momento". Otro de los puntos aclarados por José Francisco Molina fue la ausencia del brazalete de capitán en el brazo de Edrick Menjívar durante los partidos. El entrenador explicó que el portero de Olimpia continúa siendo el capitán de Honduras , pero que existe una razón específica para que otro futbolista porte la cinta. "El capitán de la selección es Menjívar. Lo que pasa que hemos decidido que el brazalete lo porte otro compañero porque solo el capitán se puede dirigir al árbitro. Él mismo dijo que era mejor que lo llevara otro jugador que pueda estar más cerca del árbitro". La palabra "fracaso" también apareció durante la conferencia de prensa, en referencia al hecho de no haber conseguido el objetivo en la competición. Molina rechazó utilizar ese término para definir lo ocurrido y aseguró que Honduras continuará con el proceso trazado. "Yo no lo llamo fracaso. El fracaso lo puedes llamar tú, yo lo respeto... Yo lo llamo: esto es parte del proceso, seguimos trabajando. No conseguimos el objetivo, es verdad. Pero esto no nos va a apartar del proceso y no nos va a apartar del camino que queremos llevar". Finalmente, Molina habló sobre su continuidad al frente de la Selección de Honduras y dejó claro que mantiene la convicción de seguir trabajando con la mirada puesta en el Mundial de 2030: "Si tú quieres conseguir algo tienes que seguir un camino, ese camino es el proceso. Y lo que queremos conseguir es clasificar para el Mundial 2030, que es el objetivo importante. Seguimos convencidos de que en algún momento las críticas tornarán en otra cosa."

data.title: ¡Bombazo! Jugador de Honduras renuncia a la Selección Nacional
data.description: Bombazo en la Selección Nacional de Honduras. Luego del fracaso de la H, que quedó fuera de los cuartos de final de la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf, se conoció una sorprendente noticia tras el empate 1-1 ante Jamaica en Tegucigalpa. Honduras evitó el ridículo de descender a la Liga B de la Concacaf, pero no pudo conseguir el boleto a los cuartos de final. Y horas después del encuentro ante los jamaiquinos trascendió una noticia que sacude al entorno de la Bicolor: Víctor Vandenbroucke ha tomado la decisión de no volver a representar a la Selección de Honduras. El joven futbolista formó parte de la convocatoria realizada por el técnico español José Francisco Molina para esta edición de la Liga de Naciones, pero para sorpresas de muchos no disputó ningún minuto durante los cuatro partidos de Honduras en el torneo. La decisión ha sido comunicada por su madre, Sarahí Vallecillo, quien envió una carta a la Federación de Fútbol de Honduras (FFH) durante el pasado fin de semana. En el documento, según trascendió, se confirmó que el juvenil atenderá el llamado de la Selección Sub-23 de Bélgica. Además, el futbolista estaría próximo a dar un importante paso en su carrera a nivel de clubes, ya que subiría al primer equipo del Gent y tendría la posibilidad de sumar minutos en la Primera División de Bélgica. La situación representa un giro importante para Vandenbroucke. Antes de incorporarse a la Selección de Honduras, el futbolista había rechazado convocatorias de la Sub-17 de Estados Unidos y de la Sub-23 de Bélgica para apostar por representar al país de sus raíces. Sin embargo, su experiencia con la Bicolor durante esta fecha FIFA habría generado molestia en su entorno familiar, especialmente por la falta de oportunidades dentro del terreno de juego. “Señor, ¿para qué convocan jugadores solo para que vayan a perder el tiempo? Mejor que los dejen donde están, continuando con su vida”, publicó Sarahí Vallecillo en redes sociales, cuestionando la decisión de convocar a su hijo. La molestia surgió luego de que Vandenbroucke no sumara ningún minuto en los cuatro encuentros disputados por Honduras en la Liga de Naciones. Incluso, en algunos de los compromisos el futbolista tuvo que observar los partidos desde las graderías. Para el duelo entre Honduras y Jamaica, disputado este lunes en el Estadio Nacional Chelato Uclés de Tegucigalpa, Vandenbroucke ni siquiera apareció entre los futbolistas suplentes. A pesar de ello, su familia decidió permanecer en el estadio para acompañarlo y mostrarle su respaldo en un momento que podría marcar el final de su etapa con la Selección Nacional de Honduras. De esta manera, Víctor Vandenbroucke estará cerrando su capítulo con la Bicolor y enfocándose en nuevos retos tanto a nivel de clubes como de selecciones nacionales.

data.title: Médicos cumplen 29 días sin consultas por salarios atrasados en Honduras
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. Las asambleas informativas de los médicos cumplen este lunes 5 de octubre 29 días y mantienen suspendidas las consultas externas y especializadas en hospitales públicos del país, debido al reclamo por el pago de salarios atrasados. La suspensión de labores comenzó el 7 de septiembre y, según lo previsto, continuará hasta el miércoles 14 de octubre, cuando se contempla una nueva reunión entre representantes del Gobierno y la junta directiva del Colegio Médico de Honduras (CMH). En ese contexto, el gremio convocó este lunes a otra jornada de asambleas informativas. El conflicto ha dejado a 27,303 ciudadanos sin atención y alrededor de 3,000 cirugías canceladas , las cuales se suman a la mora quirúrgica que arrastra el sistema sanitario desde meses atrás. Los pacientes que tenían citas programadas también han resultado afectados por la suspensión. A nueve meses del inicio del actual Gobierno, los médicos reclaman el pago de salarios atrasados de hasta nueve meses. El reclamo se mantiene después de aproximadamente seis reuniones con las autoridades, sin que, según el gremio, se haya concretado una solución. La Sesal sostiene que el salario ya fue cancelado al 95 % del personal de salud y que unos 300 médicos permanecen en proceso de pago. El CMH, por su parte, reporta alrededor de 400 profesionales pendientes de recibir sus salarios, con atrasos de entre dos y ocho meses, además de pagos relacionados con el Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) y vacaciones. Héctor Carranza, miembro de la junta directiva del CMH, afirmó que la deuda con los médicos ha avanzado un 60 % en comparación con la deuda inicial. También señaló que el 21 % de los médicos de salud pública son contratados por interinato y que ese grupo es al que se le adeudan pagos. Advirtió que las asambleas continuarán si no se cancela a todos los profesionales pendientes. La suspensión de las consultas también ha afectado a pacientes como María Velásquez, de 80 años, quien llegó al Hospital Escuela para dar seguimiento a su condición de salud, pero encontró que su cita había sido reprogramada para diciembre. “Bien me muero esperando”, expresó mientras esperaba a su hija. Velásquez, quien padece diabetes, relató que un mes antes había sufrido una emergencia relacionada con esa enfermedad y acudió al Hospital Escuela para continuar con su seguimiento médico, pero no recibió atención debido a las asambleas. También aseguró que buscó su medicamento en la farmacia, pero no pudo obtenerlo porque no había existencias. Según su relato, utiliza 20 unidades de insulina por la mañana y 10 por la noche. En el Instituto Hondureño de Seguridad Social (IHSS), las autoridades informaron de un acuerdo para suspender las asambleas y restablecer la atención normal a partir del 12 de octubre, luego de asegurar que el personal médico de la institución cuenta con el pago de sus salarios. Víctor Martínez, director ejecutivo del IHSS, indicó que durante el conflicto fueron suspendidas 115,000 citas, mientras que en el Hospital Escuela se registraron 12,500 consultas suspendidas. La atención médica continúa siendo uno de los principales puntos de presión entre el gremio y las autoridades mientras se acerca el Feriado Morazánico . El CMH mantiene el reclamo por los salarios pendientes y advierte que las asambleas informativas continuarán hasta que se complete el pago a los médicos.

data.title: Tabla posiciones Concacaf Nations League: Honduras eliminada, pero sigue en la A y Guatemala sorprende
data.description: La Selección de Honduras quedó eliminada de los cuartos de final de la Concacaf Nations League , pero logró mantener la categoría en la Liga A del torneo del área gracias al sufrido empate contra Jamaica en la última jornada del Grupo B. Tras el empate 1-1 entre Martinica y El Salvador , la Bicolor tenía esperanzas de avanzar a la siguiente ronda, toda vez que Guatemala no ganara a Surinam . Sin embargo, la debacle de Honduras se consumó antes del pitazo inicial en Tegucigalpa. Guatemala hizo su trabajo y venció por 1-0 a Surinam para quedarse con el liderato de la tabla de posiciones del Grupo B con 7 puntos. Así, los chapines se clasificaron de manera directa a los cuartos de final de la Nations League. En el estadio Nacional Chelato Uclés, Honduras y Jamaica igualaron 1-1, un resultado que dejó afuera a Surinam de los cuartos de final. Tanto chapines, jamaicanos y surinameses sumaron 7 puntos, pero Guatemala y los Reggae Boyz quedaron arriba por mejor diferencia de goles. Honduras , por su parte, terminó en el cuarto lugar de la clasificación con 4 puntos, también emparejado con Martinica y El Salvador , pero los catrachos acabaron con mejor diferencia de goles. Así, los caribeños y salvadoreños descendieron a la Liga B.

data.title: Hallan medicamentos vencidos y equipo médico de la Sesal a la intemperie en Tegucigalpa
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras . Medicamentos vencidos y equipo médico expuesto al sol, la lluvia y la humedad fueron encontrados este lunes 5 de octubre en una bodega de la Secretaría de Salud (Sesal), ubicada en el sector de El Lolo, en la capital. La situación quedó evidenciada luego del ingreso de medios de comunicación al predio, donde videos y fotografías documentaron las condiciones en que permanecen cajas de medicamentos , mobiliario y equipo médico. Las imágenes muestran una cantidad de cajas y equipos colocados en áreas expuestas a las condiciones ambientales. Entre los productos encontrados también había medicamentos que ya habían alcanzado su fecha de vencimiento . Ante los cuestionamientos por el manejo de los bienes de Salud , especialmente por las necesidades de medicamentos e insumos que enfrentan algunos centros asistenciales, el viceministro de Salud, Eduardo Midence, negó que el equipo médico esté abandonado o almacenado de manera permanente. Midence explicó que los equipos forman parte de un proyecto financiado mediante un préstamo del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID), cuya entrega se realiza de manera escalonada a diferentes establecimientos de salud. Según el funcionario, parte del mobiliario está destinado al fortalecimiento del bloque materno-infantil que se construye en Santa Rosa de Copán . Otros equipos serán enviados a establecimientos de salud seleccionados dentro del mismo proyecto. Ante las condiciones observadas en la bodega, el viceministro insistió en que los equipos no han sido abandonados ni se han deteriorado. “Se va a entregar y se está entregando, no se ha venido, no se ha almacenado o echado a perder”, aseguró. data.title: MP: "Ni siquiera recibimos el 1% del presupuesto que la Constitución ordena"
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. El Ministerio Público (MP) reclama un aumento de su presupuesto para contratar fiscales, detectives, investigadores y personal especializado que permita fortalecer la investigación y persecución penal en Honduras, informó el fiscal general adjunto, Marcio Cabañas. El funcionario señaló que la institución enfrenta limitaciones presupuestarias que dificultan ampliar su personal y desarrollar nuevos procesos de contratación. "Esperemos que a través del Congreso Nacional y la Secretaría de Finanzas  podamos tener una respuesta positiva, la Constitución de la República habla del 3%, de l Presupuesto General de la República asignado a la institución, y actualmente ni siquiera se nos da el uno por ciento", apuntó. Cabañas insistió en que un incremento presupuestario resulta necesario para abrir nuevos concursos y ampliar el recurso humano del ente fiscal. "Tiene que haber un aumento al presupuesto, sin aumento al presupuesto no hay concurso para fiscales, ni para detectives, ni para otro personal que es necesario dentro del Ministerio Público", explicó. El presupuesto asignado al Ministerio Público para el ejercicio fiscal 2026 asciende a 3,040 millones de lempiras . El fiscal general Pablo Emilio Reyes explicó que actualmente el Ministerio Público cuenta con aproximadamente 796 fiscales, pero considera necesario elevar esa cifra hasta cerca de 900 para atender las necesidades de la población y la demanda en materia de persecución penal. "Hoy contamos aproximadamente con 796 fiscales. Ocupamos el doble o el triple de fiscales para hacer frente a esta delincuencia, estamos hablando, más o menos, de unos 900", detalló Reyes. El funcionario también señaló que desde 2016 no se realiza un concurso para incorporar nuevos fiscales , una situación que ha limitado el crecimiento del personal encargado de desarrollar investigaciones y ejercer la acción penal. Cabañas destacó la necesidad de reforzar las áreas vinculadas con la investigación criminal y las ciencias forenses para fortalecer la persecución penal pública a nivel nacional. Ante las solicitudes oficiales, Elky Alvarado, vicepresidenta de la Asociación de Fiscales de Honduras , advirtió que la falta de fondos también afecta la eficiencia del Ministerio Público. "La falta de presupuesto afecta no solamente la contratación del Ministerio Fiscal, que es elemental tener el recurso humano especializado, también afecta la operatividad del Ministerio Público cuando no hay reactivos para las pruebas químicas, cuando no hay suficientes peritos, sean financistas, sean contables, sean de documentología, de marcas patrones y de cualquier otra especialidad forense", lamentó. La vicepresidenta de la Asociación de Fiscales de Honduras agregó que el ente no cuenta con suficientes peritos forenses para desarrollar investigaciones científicas que permitan fortalecer los casos ante los tribunales y calificó como "brutal" la carga que enfrenta cada fiscal.

data.title: Hallan decapitado a un hombre en su propia casa en Lepaterique
data.description: Lepaterique, Francisco Morazán. Un hombre identificado preliminarmente como Timoteo Castillo fue encontrado sin vida este lunes dentro de su vivienda en la aldea El Naranjo, municipio de Lepaterique, Francisco Morazán. De acuerdo con el reporte preliminar, el hallazgo ocurrió luego de que personas de la zona descubrieran el cuerpo de Castillo en el interior de su casa. La víctima presentaba múltiples mutilaciones y, según la información de las autoridades hasta el momento, había sufrido la amputación de la cabeza, las manos y los pies. El hecho ha generado zozobra entre los habitantes de la comunidad de El Naranjo, debido a la violencia y las condiciones en que fue encontrado el cuerpo de esta persona. Tras el levantamiento, los restos fueron trasladados hasta la morgue de Tegucigalpa, donde se realizarán los procedimientos forenses correspondientes. Las autoridades deberán establecer las circunstancias en las que ocurrió el crimen y determinar quiénes serían los responsables. Hasta el momento no se han informado detalles sobre posibles sospechosos, ni sobre el móvil del homicidio. La investigación de la Policía deberá esclarecer el violento hecho registrado en esta comunidad de Lepaterique.

data.title: Dos gigantes se interesan en Mauricio Dubón y sorprenden al hondureño
data.description: Mauricio Dubón está viviendo una temporada enorme con los Bravos de Atlanta , disputando la serie divisional donde están igualados 1-1 frente a los Dodgers de Los Ángeles . El catracho está siendo pretendido por dos de las grandes franquicias de las Grandes Ligas. Los últimos reportes indican que los Yankees de New York , el mejor equipo de la MLB, así como los Dodgers de Los Ángeles , actuales campeones, están siguiendo los pasos de Dubón, quien al ser un jugador utility, tiene muchas opciones para jugar en el roster debido a que se desempeña en seis posiciones. "Desde agosto comenzaron a surgir reportes que apuntan al interés de Nueva York por encontrar alternativas para una posición que ha estado marcada por la irregularidad. Anthony Volpe y José Caballero tuvieron una campaña complicada, con lesiones e inconsistencias que obligarían a los Yankees a evaluar diferentes escenarios de cara a 2027", reporta el Diario AS de México . Mauricio estará en la agencia libre al finalizar la temporada, seguramente ganará otro guante de oro luego de su gran actuación con los Bravos de Atlanta, sería el tercero en su carrera y por su posición de utility player es uno de los peloteros con un salario muy alto, además, un equipo que lo contrate, corre el riesgo de que no sabe si lo pueda utilizar. Dubón no está únicamente en la agenda de los Yankees de New York, también está en la órbita de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, además está la posible renovación con los Bravos de Atlanta, pero estará condicionada a recibir un salario más alto ya que en este momento es el utility mejor pagado de Grandes Ligas. Cada actuación de Dubón mejora su contrato, pues esta fue una de las razones por las que dejó los Astros de Houston ya que los texanos no pudieron seguir pagando el alto salario del hondureño. Las franquicias como Yankees y Dodgers sí tienen como pagarlo, pero Bravos estaría negociando una renovación. "Además, su situación contractual podría convertirlo en una alternativa interesante. Dubón percibe actualmente 6.1 millones de dólares y será agente libre en 2027. Mientras tanto, Volpe y Caballero deberán pasar por procesos de arbitraje salarial, lo que podría incrementar el costo de mantener a ambos jugadores", sigue explicando la nota de AS México.
