data.title: OMV top management meets with Romanian president, interim PM
data.description: A delegation from the natural gas company OMV, one of the largest players in Romania's energy market, met with president Nicușor Dan and acting prime minister Ilie Bolojan on Monday, October 5. Emma Delaney, new OMV CEO, led the delegation that first met with the president. According to diplomatic sources cited by ProTV , the two discussed when gas production from the Neptun Deep field will actually begin and then enter the transmission system, as well as what this project will mean for Romania’s energy security. The first gas is expected to enter the national network in the first half of next year, according to the company. During the subsequent meeting with the prime minister, OMV representatives discussed developments in the energy sector amid fluctuations in fuel prices driven by international conflicts and supply crises. An important point of this discussion referred to the Neptun Deep project as well. Bolojan emphasized the importance of natural gas resources in the Black Sea for the Romanian economy, which will contribute to strengthening national energy security. “The completion of the investment and the start of gas extraction in the Neptun Deep field must remain government priorities so that Romania can capitalize on the resources in the Black Sea for the benefit of the national economy and the entire region. We must find operational cooperation formulas to ensure convergence of action in this strategic project for both parties,” acting prime minister Ilie Bolojan said. The new OMV head, Emma Delaney, was named Chairwoman of the Executive Board and CEO of the company as of September 1. She is also Chairwoman of the Supervisory Board of OMV Petrom and Vice Chairwoman of the Supervisory Board of Borouge Group International AG. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Economics and Business from Trinity College Dublin and a master’s degree in management from ESCP Europe. A native English speaker, she is also fluent in French and German. With extensive experience in the international energy industry, Delaney has strong leadership expertise in both the upstream and downstream sectors. She is recognized for her strategic perspective, extensive commercial skills, and collaborative leadership style. Before joining the OMV Group, Delaney served as Executive Vice President, Customers and Products, while also being a member of BP’s Executive Committee. In this position, she globally coordinated a portfolio that included fuels, convenience stores, biofuels, aviation fuels, advanced lubricants, and electric vehicle charging solutions. Delaney played a key role in transforming BP’s Customers and Products division, focusing on operational excellence, portfolio optimization, and value creation. Throughout her 30-year career at BP, she held senior leadership positions in the company’s upstream and downstream operations and coordinated complex transformation programs across rapidly evolving markets and regions. Her international experience covers Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Asia-Pacific region. Christina Verchere, CEO of OMV Petrom, the Romanian subsidiary of the Vienna-based energy company, also comes from BP, having served as BP’s Regional President for Canada, based in Calgary, and between 2014 and 2018 as BP’s Regional President for Asia Pacific, based in Jakarta, Indonesia, before coming to Romania in 2018.

data.title: Social Monitor: Romanians more worried about declining living standards than most EU citizens
data.description: Declining living standards and poverty are among Romanians’ leading economic concerns, with worries significantly higher than the European Union averages, according to Eurobarometer data analysed by the Social Monitor , a project of Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung Romania. Some 62% of Romanian respondents expressed concern about falling living standards, compared with 40% across the EU, while 48% were worried about poverty, versus a European average of 32%. The findings placed Romania among the EU countries where economic insecurity is most pronounced. Poland recorded considerably lower levels of concern, with 36% of respondents worried about declining living standards and 21% about poverty. Asked which goods and services they feared they might be unable to afford over the next 12 months, 45% of Romanians mentioned travel. Utilities and medical care followed, each cited by 44% of respondents. Romania’s level of concern about utility bills was exceeded only by Ireland, at 47%, and Greece, at 58%, the report revealed. Meanwhile, 40% of Romanian respondents said they feared being unable to afford food, a share close to those recorded in Ireland, Greece, and Portugal. By contrast, basic expenses such as food, housing, and utilities were less prominent concerns in Germany, France, and Italy, where respondents were more worried about discretionary spending, including travel, entertainment, and eating out. Meanwhile, half of Romanian respondents described the country’s current economic situation as poor, while 25% considered it neither good nor bad and slightly more than one-fifth rated it positively. The results were broadly in line with the EU averages of 49%, 25% and 24%, respectively. Assessments of personal finances were also close to the European average. Some 34% of Romanians described their economic situation as good, 38% as neither good nor bad, and 27% as poor. According to the same analysis, Romanians were divided over the prospects of the next generation. While 42% believed today’s children would have a lower standard of living than their parents when they reach adulthood, 35% expected them to be better off. This made Romania more pessimistic than several other eastern EU countries. Only around 26-27% of respondents in Bulgaria, Hungary, and Poland expected the next generation to have a lower standard of living.

The results were broadly in line with the EU averages of 49%, 25% and 24%, respectively. Assessments of personal finances were also close to the European average. Some 34% of Romanians described their economic situation as good, 38% as neither good nor bad, and 27% as poor. According to the same analysis, Romanians were divided over the prospects of the next generation. While 42% believed today’s children would have a lower standard of living than their parents when they reach adulthood, 35% expected them to be better off. This made Romania more pessimistic than several other eastern EU countries. Only around 26-27% of respondents in Bulgaria, Hungary, and Poland expected the next generation to have a lower standard of living.

data.title: Over half of Romanians turn to AI first for health information, PwC survey finds
data.description: More than half of Romanian consumers use artificial intelligence (AI) tools as their first source of health and wellness information, according to PwC’s Voice of the Consumer 2026 survey. The share reached 53% in Romania, compared with 47% in Central and Eastern Europe and 51% globally. The survey found that 36% of Romanian respondents would use AI to create personalised fitness or wellness plans, while 31% were open to using it for meal planning, shopping lists, and nutrition advice. A similar proportion would rely on the technology to identify potential sleep- or stress-related problems, while 29% would use it for a preliminary assessment based on symptoms. “Romanian consumers’ openness to using AI for health and wellness-related matters also reflects more limited access to medical consultations,” said Adina Vizoli, Health & Pharma Leader at PwC Romania. However, 54% of Romanian respondents cited insufficient disposable income as the main obstacle to meeting their health and wellness objectives, compared with 47% globally. Lower-cost options were therefore more common, with 72% of respondents purchasing vitamins and supplements and 38% choosing specialised healthy foods and beverages. By comparison, 23% paid for preventive medical check-ups, 19% for gym memberships, and 16% for fitness equipment. Only 15% had purchased health or fitness applications or subscriptions, while 13% had paid for psychological support, including counselling and meditation apps. Another 12% had purchased spa experiences or treatments. According to the same survey, a longer and healthier life was the leading objective among Romanian respondents, followed by reducing stress and improving mental health. Despite this, only 39% said they exercised frequently, compared with 44% across the regional sample and 58% globally. The survey also found that 32% of Romanians rated their health as good or excellent. The use of GLP-1 medication remained limited, although approximately one in four respondents said they were considering using such treatments in the future. PwC collected the data between February and March 2026 from 21,808 respondents in 27 countries. The Romanian sample comprised 707 people, while the Central and Eastern European results covered 2,419 respondents from Romania, Poland, Hungary, and Ukraine.

data.title: Independent PM-designate Luca Niculescu received with reluctance by parties in Romania
data.description: Unlike his predecessors, Niculescu’s designation has not immediately polarised the centrist parties that could potentially form his parliamentary majority. However, moving from the first reaction to sufficient parliamentary support may prove complicated. The designation of an independent candidate may indicate that no parliamentary majority emerged among the centrist parties during consultations. “I chose the person who has the best chance of forming a majority,” president Dan said when introducing Niculescu , exactly five months after the successful no-confidence motion against the government of prime minister Ilie Bolojan and after three failed attempts to form a new government. “Mr Niculescu has the freedom to decide, after in-depth discussions with the parties, the formula of government – political or technocratic. What is important is the majority in Parliament,” Dan said. The president said he was confident that a government headed by Niculescu would preserve Romania’s pro-Western orientation while respecting the country’s fiscal targets and international commitments. Besides ticking the pro-Western commitment box, in line with the stated position of all parliamentary parties, including the eurosceptic, nationalist and far-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR), Niculescu promised “careful use of public money, predictable economic policies, compliance with Romania’s commitments, acceleration of investments and reforms, and a state that serves as well as possible all of its citizens”. A diplomat by profession but a journalist by education, Niculescu spent roughly two-thirds of his professional career in the media before moving into diplomacy. He has no formal background in economic or financial policy, although his role as coordinator of Romania’s OECD accession process has given him extensive contacts across government institutions. He may therefore serve as an interface for a political construction that would project its own policies – whether driven by the Presidency, a parliamentary majority or a combination of the two. Niculescu has never been a member of a political party. But first, he must secure lawmakers’ support within ten days, with both the composition of his government and the political strategy behind it remaining largely unpredictable. Niculescu’s career, which began as an intern at a radio station while a student and later took him to the head of the Romanian subsidiary of RFI and to correspondent positions for French media, reached a new level when president Klaus Iohannis appointed him Romania’s ambassador to France at the end of 2015. The ministers picked by Niculescu will define his government’s orientation The team of ministers that Niculescu proposes will be crucial in determining both the orientation of his government and its chances of securing a parliamentary majority. With no political party behind him, and no obvious possibility of being adopted by one party without antagonising others, Niculescu faces the difficult task of defining a governing strategy within a very short period. His OECD work has probably given him contacts within most ministries, but not necessarily the political leverage or economic-policy profile needed to reconcile the competing demands of the parliamentary parties. Social Democrats remained reluctant and raised the early-elections scenario The Social Democratic Party (PSD) appeared disappointed by the nomination, with party leader Sorin Grindeanu saying that president Dan “continues to defy parliamentary mathematics”. He implied that Niculescu could represent the centre-right bloc rather than the party holding the largest number of seats in Parliament. “It is the president’s choice. The Social Democratic Party makes its own decisions. Therefore, tomorrow [October 6] we will have a meeting of the National Permanent Bureau in which we will analyse this proposal,” Grindeanu wrote on Facebook on Monday evening. Earlier on Monday, during consultations with president Dan, Grindeanu had put himself forward for the prime minister position. The majority he appeared to envisage, however, included AUR, breaching Dan’s condition against bringing the far-right party into the governing majority. Grindeanu also reiterated PSD’s intention to change the economic policies implemented in Romania over the past year, putting the party at odds with the centre-right PNL-USR-UDMR bloc. He linked PSD’s support for Niculescu to the latter’s economic policy and raised the prospect of early elections if the new candidate continues the policies of the Bolojan government. “If the designated prime minister continues to support Bolojan’s austerity policies, I believe that there is no other way to put Romania back on the right track than to go to early elections,” Grindeanu said. PNL and USR expressed openness but no unconditional support The National Liberal Party (PNL) said it “takes note” of president Dan’s decision to nominate Niculescu and will discuss the government programme, its priorities and the proposed ministerial team before deciding whether to support the investiture. “Following discussions and analysis of the government programme, the PNL will make a decision regarding the investiture vote,” party spokesman Ionel Bogdan said. Earlier on Monday, PNL leader Ilie Bolojan said the party would remain in opposition if PSD were part of the government, but left the door open to supporting a government at the investiture vote. “Being aware of the political deadlock, after the president makes the nomination, we will discuss seriously and see what the possibilities are to avoid prolonging the political deadlock,” Bolojan said. PNL had previously signalled that it was prepared to consider several options, including an alternative government or early elections. The Save Romania Union (USR) will similarly analyse Niculescu’s programme, ministerial team and the parliamentary majority supporting him, party leader Dominic Fritz said. At the same time, Fritz reiterated that USR would not support a government containing PSD ministers or controlled by PSD. UDMR offered the clearest opening – but it is the smallest of the centrist parties too The Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania (UDMR) appeared to offer Niculescu the clearest opening for parliamentary support, although it also wants to see how a majority can be assembled and what government programme he proposes. UDMR lawmakers could vote for Niculescu as prime minister, the party’s parliamentary leader Csoma Botond said. The party’s only “red line” is that it will not negotiate with AUR or SOS Romania to form a majority. “We can vote for Mr Luca Niculescu. Let’s see how this majority can be formed and let’s see what government programme Mr Luca Niculescu would propose,” Csoma said. “If we can avoid getting into this situation, we could certainly vote for a government led by Luca Niculescu.” The UDMR position leaves open the possibility of reviving a broader centre-right coalition, but such a formula would still need to attract PSD support or sufficient individual lawmakers from outside the four-party bloc. The previous PNL-USR-UDMR government proposal led by Siegfried Mureșan secured only 182 votes in Parliament , well below the 233 needed for investiture.

data.title: Romania's Romgaz prepares to restart fertiliser producer Azomures after takeover
data.description: Employees have already returned to the platform and are carrying out the work needed to prepare the installations for a restart targeted for April 2027. “Romgaz employees are preparing for the restart of the installations, which will take place in April 2027. There are certain works being carried out to put the installations in good working order, tests are being conducted, and all the procedures required to start the installations are being followed, so that we are ready by April 1,” Emil Almășan, leader of the Alternativa 2002 trade union, told Radio Tg. Mureș, as reported by Profit.ro . Romgaz, which took over the Azomures chemical plant, is asking shareholders to approve a new EUR 100 million credit line, as the operations acquired from the plant are not expected to generate revenues or cash inflows until April 2027.

data.title: Romania’s wheat, barley and triticale crop up 14% y/y to 13.5 mln tonnes
data.description: Farmers had harvested more than 13.5 million tonnes of wheat, rye and triticale by August 31, compared with the 2025 output reported by the National Institute of Statistics in its final data. The increase came as the area cultivated with the three crops expanded by 48,900 hectares to 2.4 mln hectares, Economica.net reported. Winter barley and two-row barley production reached 3.9 mln tonnes, up from 2.8 mln tonnes a year earlier. By August 31, 99.4% of the area under winter barley and 99.8% of the area under emmer barley had been harvested. The area cultivated with the two barley crops increased by 14% from 2025 to 716,200 hectares. The oilseed rape harvest was also almost complete, with 99.8% of the cultivated area harvested by August 31. Production reached 2.7 mln tonnes, 19% up from 2.2 mln tonnes a year earlier.

data.title: Romania moves to streamline grain exports from local farmers through Constanta port
data.description: “Together with the minister of transport, Radu Miruță, and with representatives of railway companies and the administration of the Port of Constanta, we had a meeting with representative associations of farmers in the crop sector to find solutions to the logistical difficulties related to the export of Romanian grains,” Tanczos wrote on Facebook . “As I stated the other day, our priority is to provide Romanian farmers with the transport capacity and logistics necessary for their goods to reach export markets as efficiently as possible,” he added. The move comes amid growing pressure on Romania’s grain-export infrastructure. Poland and Romania have turned down Ukraine’s request for help moving millions of tonnes of grain trapped by Russian attacks on its Black Sea ports and shipping, Politico reported on October 4. “The interest for our own farmers remains a priority,” Tanczos said. Surplus Ukrainian grain, combined with low water levels on the Danube, is already putting additional pressure on Romanian ports and making it more difficult for local farmers to sell their crops. “Everybody knows we cannot double the number of trains, we cannot double the roads, railways and port capacity,” he said. “It is what it is.” According to Tanczos, the discussions focused on removing administrative blockages and logistical bottlenecks in order to improve the organisation of transport and facilitate the export of Romanian agri-food products through the Port of Constanta. Transport minister Radu Miruță said the meeting resulted in an agreement to amend the order approving the regime for accepting freight trains at railway stations serving the Constanta seaport. The changes are intended to shorten the time required to issue port acceptance for trains awaiting unloading, improve coordination among operators transporting goods to the port and introduce a more effective mechanism for sanctioning those that fail to comply with the rules. “The necessary regulatory changes will be implemented expeditiously by the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure in the immediate future,” Miruță said.

data.title: Romania's carmaker Dacia suspends production for two days on weak orders
data.description: “We confirm the stoppage of production on October 9 and 12,” Dacia representatives told Profit.ro . According to union representatives, the production halt is related to the volume of orders received by the plant, following an earlier slowdown in production after the summer holiday period. The plant is currently producing just over 1,000 vehicles per day, according to Profit.ro, compared with maximum capacity of around 1,300 vehicles per day. The lower production rate has already prompted the factory to adjust its shift structure. “The shutdown is another issue, and it comes from the fact that the number of orders this month and the production mix are lower. It took two days of shutdown to adjust production to the order book,” Viorel Ungureanu, leader of the Dacia Car Union, told Profit.ro. “For now, we have no visibility for the future, but we hope that another shutdown will not be necessary. We discuss with management frequently, and we do not believe that there will be another shutdown this year,” he added. Dacia’s suppliers curtail operations in response. Dacia’s lower production has also affected suppliers. Employees at Horse Romania’s gearbox and aluminium manufacturing departments, as well as support, quality and logistics staff, interrupted their activity on September 24, 25 and 28 because of lower orders from its main client, Automobile Dacia, according to information obtained by Profit.ro . The employees were sent home and received 85% of their normal salary, together with meal vouchers, for the days they did not work. Maintenance and repair work was carried out around the gearbox assembly lines. The rest of the plant continued to operate normally, with the engine department maintaining its usual production level and supplying engines to all Dacia plants. Dacia’s vehicle production has fallen by more than 14% this year, with almost 160,000 vehicles assembled in the first eight months, according to Profit.ro. Dacia Romania head Mihai Bordeanu confirmed during the launch of the new-generation Dacia Spring that the plant was heading for a double-digit production decline this year, citing the unfavourable conditions in the automotive market.

data.title: Romania loses to Sweden in fourth straight Nations League defeat
data.description: Romania’s national football team lost 1-0 to Sweden at Bucharest’s National Arena on Monday, October 5, recording its fourth consecutive defeat in UEFA Nations League Group B4. Arsenal striker Viktor Gyökeres scored the match’s only goal in the 13th minute, extending his scoring run to seven consecutive Nations League appearances for Sweden, Agerpres reported. Romania lost all four matches played during the current international window: 2-1 away to Sweden on September 25, 4-2 at home to Bosnia and Herzegovina on September 28 , 6-0 away to Poland on October 2, and 1-0 at home to Sweden. Head coach Gheorghe Hagi acknowledged that Romania’s performance under his leadership had fallen short of his expectations but argued that rebuilding the team would require time. “I saw things differently at first, but gradually I realised that we have work to do if we want to compete with the strongest teams,” Hagi said after the match on Monday, as quoted by News.ro . “This process needs some time - a little, not a lot.” The coach said Romania showed signs of improvement against Sweden but needed greater confidence and aggression in the opposition half. He also set the ambitious goal of building a team capable of surpassing Romania’s celebrated “Golden Generation” of the 1990s. “We have had enough of talking about the previous generation. It must be surpassed. That is the only objective that still stands - to build a better team than the Golden Generation,” Hagi said. He added that he would discuss his position with the Romanian Football Federation’s leadership within two days. “Give me a little time. If I cannot do it, I will go home. I have lost four matches - I should hardly even be speaking. I do not like losing,” he said. Romania will play its final two group fixtures in November, hosting Poland on November 14 before travelling to face Bosnia and Herzegovina on November 17.

data.description: Romanian president Nicușor Dan appointed independent Luca Niculescu on Monday, October 5, to “harmonize positions” expressed by political parties and form a new government. “The choice came following today’s consultations . I chose the person who has the best chances of securing a majority. Over the past four years, he has been working on Romania’s accession process to the OECD; he has worked for the Romanian state,” Nicușor Dan said. Niculescu will now have to hold talks with parliamentary parties and form a majority “deeply anchored in the Western direction,” according to the PM-designate. “I will hold talks with the parliamentary parties to build a majority and agree on a realistic government program. I will not promise miracles, but what I can promise is seriousness in the use of public money, predictability for the economy, respect for commitments, accelerating reforms and a state that functions as well as possible,” Niculescu said. https://www.facebook.com/NicusorDan.ro/videos/1647713663377984 Who is Luca Niculescu? Born on April 25, 1971, in Bucharest, Luca Niculescu graduated from the Faculty of Journalism and Communication Sciences at the University of Bucharest (1995) and holds a master’s degree in European Journalism from the University Centre for Journalism in Strasbourg (1996). According to Digi24 , between 1992 and 2016, Luca Niculescu worked as a journalist. He was editor-in-chief of RFI Romania, as well as a program host on several television stations: Money Channel, TVR 1, Digi24. Mainly specialized in international relations, he had a weekly column in Dilema Veche for five years. At the same time, he was a permanent correspondent in Romania for French media outlets (France Info, France Culture, France Inter, TV5, and the daily newspaper Libération). Between 2016 and 2022, Luca Niculescu was Romania’s Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to France, the Principality of Monaco and the Principality of Andorra. In this capacity, he also represented Romania in relations with international organizations based in Paris, particularly the OECD and the International Organisation of La Francophonie. He was also president of the Group of Francophone Ambassadors in France (GAFF) between 2019 and 2022. Since September 2022, Luca Niculescu has been secretary of state at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and National Coordinator for Romania’s accession process to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). Context This is the fourth nomination made by the Romanian president. So far, Nicușor Dan has designated Eugen Tomac, who stepped down, and Adrian Veștea and Siegfried Mureșan, who failed to obtain a vote of confidence from Parliament. Before Monday’s consultations, political sources cited by Digi24 indicated that Social Democratic leader Sorin Grindeanu and Liberal-backed interim finance minister Alexandru Nazare were among the options being discussed for the position of prime minister. However, that quickly changed before the president’s announcement in the evening. Gathering support Prime minister-designate Luca Niculescu has 10 days to present the list of ministers and the government program and to request a vote of confidence from parliament. To be invested, he needs 233 votes. Political parties were careful with their initial statements regarding Niculescu. The leader of the far-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians party (AUR), George Simion, said that the PM-designate is “also a puppet,” and will therefore receive “zero votes from AUR.” In turn, Petrișor Peiu, one of AUR’s leaders, announced that the party’s MPs will not vote for the government that prime minister-designate Luca Niculescu will propose, stressing that AUR will not participate in the vote. The Social Democrats said, through the voice of the party president, that the new nomination “continues to defy parliamentary mathematics.” “After four right-wing prime ministers have failed, we are seeing another appointment that does not take into account the party that won the elections. It is the president’s choice,” Sorin Grindeanu wrote on his Facebook page . The PSD leader said that the Social Democrats' National Permanent Bureau will hold a meeting on Tuesday, October 6, to analyze the new possible government. “If the prime minister-designate continues to support Bolojan’s austerity policies, I believe there is no other way to put Romania back on the right path than to hold early elections. I want to put an end to Romania’s interim governments!” the Social Democratic leader also said. Finally, the spokesman of the National Liberal Party, Ionel Bogdan, said that the formation took note of the nomination. He added that PNL will hold talks with Niculescu and analyze the forthcoming government program before making a decision regarding the investiture vote. Save Romania Union Party (USR) president Dominic Fritz said he welcomes the nomination of Luca Niculescu for the position of prime minister, but added that his party will not vote for a government that includes PSD ministers. “He is a respected diplomat, renowned for the professional execution of the missions entrusted to him, for example, Romania’s accession process to the OECD. USR will analyze the program, the team of ministers, and the majority supporting him. We will discuss with the prime minister-designate how he intends to ensure that the government can deliver results, as USR ministers have delivered,” Fritz said on his Facebook page. https://www.facebook.com/dominicprimar/posts/pfbid02ncv5juBLUjanPhRkaXfpAdML9TUBq9tPnAxKy8Q8eD4ya8DtJGG6778cwPMq1hMtl

data.title: Public Affairs Solutions appoints Decebal Mohirta as Managing Associate
data.description: Decebal joined Public Affairs Solutions in 2021 and has progressed from Junior Consultant to Senior Government Relations Associate, gradually taking on the coordination of complex accounts and projects in sectors such as healthcare and the pharmaceutical industry, defense, education, and FMCG. In his new role, his responsibilities will include coordinating projects and teams, developing client relationships, and contributing to the company's commercial and regional growth. In recent years, a significant portion of his work has focused on public affairs projects in the healthcare sector. These include the "Democratization of Robotic Surgery" campaign, which aimed to expand access for patients in the public healthcare system to robot-assisted surgery and to develop a public funding mechanism, as well as projects to include new drugs on the list of reimbursed and free medications and to overcome funding bottlenecks that were delaying patients' access to treatments. Decebal also coordinated the public affairs and stakeholder engagement component for the launch of a major industrial investment in drug manufacturing in Romania and was involved in education reform projects and initiatives regarding vaccination in pharmacies. This promotion also reflects his contribution to the business growth of Public Affairs Solutions. In 2026, the projects and new clients brought in by Decebal generated, according to the company's internal data, revenue of over 100,000 euros. Previously, he initiated the development of the Political Outlook product, designed to analyze the impact of political developments on the business environment, which was developed in part through a series of events organized in partnership with chambers of commerce and business organizations. At the same time, he contributed to the development of new services and the expansion of Public Affairs Solutions' international partnerships; through this network, the company is currently involved in projects covering more than 12 markets in Central and Eastern Europe. "Decebal's promotion is a great reflection of the professional development model we are building at Public Affairs Solutions. In the more than five years he has spent with the company, he has evolved from a consultant at the start of his career into a professional who coordinates complex projects, builds client relationships, generates business, and helps his colleagues grow. His results over the past few years, from healthcare and education projects to his role in attracting new clients and expanding our regional operations, naturally justify this step. For me, one of the greatest satisfactions as a leader is feeling that I'm able to develop leaders who are better than I am, and Decebal's journey gives me that satisfaction. In his new role, Decebal will have a broader mandate in coordinating projects, developing services, and strengthening the team and the company's regional presence." said Codrin Scutaru, CEO of Public Affairs Solutions. In recent years, Decebal has also coordinated the company's internship program, contributing to the selection, onboarding, evaluation, and mentoring processes for colleagues at the start of their careers. Decebal Mohirta began his career in advocacy and public affairs in 2017, working in civil society on projects dedicated to education and the representation of young Romanians. He served as Secretary General of the League of Romanian Students Abroad and founded the Forum of Romanian Students Everywhere, a project that received the Aspen Social Action Award in 2024. He is a graduate of the University of Konstanz, where he studied History and Political Science, and of the Executive MBA program at Beyond Business School; he is currently pursuing a master's degree in Philosophy, Politics, and Economics at the University of Bucharest. He is a member and alumnus of the Aspen Institute Romania.

data.title: Report: Over 5 million Romanians live across Europe, largest communities in UK and Italy
data.description: Approximately 5.1 million Romanians live in European countries, mostly in the United Kingdom, followed by Spain and Italy, according to official data from the Ministry of Labor analyzed by G4media.ro . The Romanian community is the largest among the communities of European citizens living in the United Kingdom. United Kingdom Currently, 1.02 million Romanians have legal residence in the United Kingdom, of whom 684,380 have obtained permanent status. Approximately 100,000 Romanians have obtained British citizenship, according to documents seen by G4media.ro. Between April 1, 2025, and March 31, 2026, around 39,000 Romanians returned to the country, with Romania ranking first in Europe in terms of the number of people leaving the United Kingdom. At the end of June 2026, 1.47 million applications from Romanian citizens had been submitted under the EU Settlement Scheme (EUSS), the scheme through which the United Kingdom granted the right of residence to EU citizens who lived in the UK before Brexit. Germany As of December 31, 2025, there were 903,770 Romanian citizens registered in Germany (6.4% of Germany’s foreign population), according to Germany’s Central Register of Foreigners. Of the Romanians living in Germany, 510,600 are men (6.9%), and 393,170 are women (5.9%). Romanians have the highest employment rate among EU citizens in Germany (72.7%), even exceeding the rate for German citizens (71%). In November 2025, 558,950 Romanians were employed (522,910 with social security contributions and 89,740 in self-employment or marginal activities). Spain As of January 1, 2025, 609,270 Romanian residents were registered in Spain, according to the Spanish National Statistics Institute (INE), and 1.1 million Romanians held a valid residence certificate. The Romanian community in Spain is the second largest, after the Moroccan community. Almost 55,000 Romanians work in Spain as self-employed workers (autónomos). At the end of April 2026, 346,290 Romanian citizens were registered as contributors to the Spanish social security system. According to data from the Spanish National Statistics Institute (INE), of the total 609,270 Romanian residents, almost 129,000 people are young – 21.16% of the community. Italy The number of Romanian residents registered in Italy in 2025 was slightly over 1 million, of whom 592,684 were women and 460,358 were men. In 2024, 598,765 Romanian workers paid employment taxes (545,433 employees, 44,970 self-employed and 8,362 project-based workers), while 53,432 were owners of individual businesses. Most Romanians in Italy work in the services sector – 15% in services provided to families/at home, 7% in hotels and restaurants (HORECA), 5.5% in commerce, 16.5% in construction and 6.1% in agriculture. No less than 42,510 Romanians were already retired in Italy. In the 2023/2024 school year, 147,926 Romanian students were enrolled in schools in Italy. France The Romanian community in France was estimated at 450,000–500,000 citizens. There are no official statistics based on ethnicity in France, as national minorities are not recognized. The data presented by the Ministry of Labor is based on estimates by the Romanian diplomatic mission in Albion. Other states Sizable Romanian communities were also in Austria (155,721), the Netherlands (63,848 official residents), Cyprus (45,000), Greece (28,250), Sweden (25,300-30,000), Denmark (17,000-20,000), and Estonia (1,000-1,500). The National Institute of Statistics announced the main demographic statistics for Romania in August, with data valid as of January 1, 2026. Romania’s resident population was 19.041 million people, down by 1,829 people compared with January 1, 2025, mainly due to deaths, according to INS. The number of immigrants exceeded the number of emigrants in 2025 by 102,200 people. The international migration balance, which increased compared with previous years, failed, however, to offset the negative natural increase.

data.title: Romanian cosmonaut Dumitru Prunariu awarded Theodore von Karman Prize
data.description: Dumitru Prunariu, the only Romanian to have flown into outer space, was awarded the Theodore von Karman Prize at the annual gala of the International Academy of Astronautics (IAA), held in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday, October 4. The distinction “recognizes outstanding achievements throughout an entire career and is named after the Academy’s founder and first president, Theodore von Karman, a leading figure in global aerospace science and engineering,” according to a statement issued by Dumitru Prunariu and cited by Agerpres . In the citation on the diploma awarded to Prunariu, the IAA highlighted a life dedicated to international astronautics: from his 1981 space flight to decades of involvement in the governance of space activities and planetary defense. Prunariu's contributions as president of the Romanian Space Agency were also highlighted, as was his promotion of multilateral cooperation through his work within the United Nations (UN), the Association of Space Explorers and other international bodies, as well as his commitment to the peaceful, responsible and cooperation-based use of outer space. “I receive this distinction with gratitude, as recognition of a life of work: a journey through engineering, space flight, leadership of national space activities, diplomacy, education and international cooperation. Throughout these different responsibilities, I was guided by one conviction: space activities can contribute to the advancement of human knowledge while also bringing nations and people closer together,” Dumitru Prunariu said. In his speech, the Romanian cosmonaut emphasized the important role the IAA has played in his own career: a community of scientific excellence, a meeting place between disciplines and cultures, and a framework for exchanging experience and developing ideas through dialogue. He highlighted the growing need for independent expertise and international cooperation at a time of rapid expansion of space activities. Finally, Prunariu reaffirmed his “commitment to protecting the planet, the sustainable use of space, the responsible conduct of lunar activities and bringing younger generations closer to science and exploration.” Founded in 1960 in Stockholm and recognized by the UN in 1996, the IAA is an independent, nongovernmental and nonprofit organization that promotes the development of astronautics for peaceful purposes and international cooperation, bringing together expertise from the fundamental sciences, engineering, life sciences and social sciences.

data.title: Turkish vessel carrying grain reportedly hit by drone near Romanian waters, two dead
data.description: A Turkish vessel carrying grain was hit by a drone in the Black Sea, near Romania’s offshore oil and gas production platform Pescăruş, operated by OMV Petrom, News.ro reported. Representatives of the Romanian Naval Authority initially announced that a fire broke out on board the ship named Royad Mammadov, while the captain was injured and 13 crew members were reported missing. No less than 11 crew members were saved after a rescue operation, and the helicopter of the General Aviation Inspectorate winched the injured persons on board in order to provide emergency medical assistance. Two deceased persons have also been identified, according to official sources . The mission is ongoing, with Coast Guard vessels and the helicopter of the General Aviation Inspectorate carrying out specific activities. “Today, around 11:00, the Romanian Naval Authority, through the Constanţa MRCC Service (Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre), was alerted about a serious maritime incident that occurred outside Romania’s territorial waters. Constanţa MRCC requested the intervention of ARSVOM and the mobilization of rescue vessels,” ANR representatives said. Several intervention units have been mobilized in response, including the “SAR APOLLO” vessel (which departed from Sulina) and “SAR ARTEMIS” (which departed from Berth 72). The intervention of the “SAR ARES” vessel was also requested. The incident was first reported approximately 20 nautical miles from the Romanian shore, while the Coast Guard indicated a position around 9 nautical miles southeast of the Pescăruş Platform.

data.title: Romanian Art Week launches across five cities this month
data.description: Romanian Art Week will hold its 2026 edition from October 17 to 25 in Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca, Timișoara, Oradea, and Craiova. The programme includes exhibitions, discussions, studio visits, and meetings with artists, curators, collectors, and other cultural professionals. In Bucharest, the event is being organised in partnership with the National Museum of Art of Romania, the Museum of Recent Art, and the National Museum of Contemporary Art. Commercial galleries, artist-run venues, and independent cultural initiatives will also participate across the five cities. The programme will cover artistic practice, collecting, cultural management, and the international circulation of contemporary art, the organizers said. Museum directors, international curators and representatives of European art weeks and cultural platforms are expected to attend, with a particular focus on Central and Eastern Europe. Romanian Art Week has also joined The Spider, a network connecting art weeks and Gallery Weekend events in cities including Amsterdam, Berlin, Brussels, London, Prague, Vienna, and Zurich. Further details can be found here .
data.translatedTitle: Romanian Art Week launches across five cities this month
data.translatedDescription: Romanian Art Week will hold its 2026 edition from October 17 to 25 in Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca, Timișoara, Oradea, and Craiova. The programme includes exhibitions, discussions, studio visits, and meetings with artists, curators, collectors, and other cultural professionals. In Bucharest, the event is being organised in partnership with the National Museum of Art of Romania, the Museum of Recent Art, and the National Museum of Contemporary Art. Commercial galleries, artist-run venues, and independent cultural initiatives will also participate across the five cities. The programme will cover artistic practice, collecting, cultural management, and the international circulation of contemporary art, the organizers said. Museum directors, international curators and representatives of European art weeks and cultural platforms are expected to attend, with a particular focus on Central and Eastern Europe. Romanian Art Week has also joined The Spider, a network connecting art weeks and Gallery Weekend events in cities including Amsterdam, Berlin, Brussels, London, Prague, Vienna, and Zurich. Further details can be found here .

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: APANHA-SE MAIS DEPRESSA UM MENTIROSO QUE UM COXO!
data.description:
DSP através da sua equipa de "Lambe-Botas" está cavando cada vez mais a sua própria cova, adiantando cada vez mais o seu fim. Somente alguns acreditavam que foi ele quem estava por trás do "Progresso Nacional" o blog onde começou toda essa história de Mentiras, Calunias, Difamações, Ameaças e tantos outros agressões tóxicas ao espírito humano, a todos os que não estão do seu lado e cujo o único objectivo, era ser chamado de rei dos réis da Guiné. Comandou o Progresso Nacional assim como Bin Laden comandou a Al-Qaeda e acabou por fracassar. Pensou, repensou e resolveu voltar novamente ainda com mais TERROR e está a comandar o Guiné Puro tentando levar toda a nação ao abismo assim como o ISIS quer levar a humanidade. Camaradas, Guiné Puro assim como o falecido Progresso Nacional é o reflexo do espirito de DSP, alí é possivel ver tudo e quanto o sujeito é baixo. DSP é um hipócrita e um anarquista moderno. "ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E COMPRAS?!" essa foi uma das frases da recente publicação que mostram por quem e para que fim, é dirigido o Guiné Puro ou melhor o blog do terror como podem ver já a seguir. Demonstraram mais uma vez claramente que o "MCCI" pertence a DPS, pois uma publicação dessa no próprio blog do ganancioso só pode ser das duas uma: "Boca capli elis ou Foronta passanta e dicidi ca sucundi rostu". Camaradas, Domingos Simões Pereira afundou seu próprio barco devido a sua ganância e complexo de superioridade. "I pirigu pa i faladu ba cuma, el i unicu alguim cu bai escola na Guiné" seu ultimo desejo é "afundar com todos, inclusive o PAIGC". __________PARA A VOSSA CONFIRMAÇÃO, AQUI ESTÁ A PUBLICAÇÃO_________ MARCOS GALINA BARBOSA VAI PERCEBER QUE METEU COM GENTE
PERSISTENTE. BÔ DISSAL I NA BIN FASSI PASSSAÇÃO LI. tUDO PUBLICAÇÕES KU I FASSI
I NA RESP+UNDI PAREL. NIN IKANA SEDU DIDIA. NONA VINGAL MANERA KU NÓ PUDI. JÁ
TEMOS ALGUÉM NO AEROPORTO PARA NOS INFOMAR O DIA EM QUE EL CHEGAR. INVENTOU
AGRESSÃO E NESTE MOMENTO ESTÁ EM QUELUZ EM PORTUGAL. FILHO DA PUTA. MENTIROSO
COMO OS TEUS PATRÕES OS SUJOS JOMAV E BRAIMA CAMARÁ. MARCOS GALINA, BU NA
ARREPENDI. PERA BU DJUBI. ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E
COMPRAS?! VAMOS PROVAR DEPOIS. FIDJU DI BALETA Olá a todos, ainda bem que descobriram
que o Pirata informático- hackec é o Marcos Galina Barbosa, Eng. Informático.
Tentei várias vezes avisar o Ticha Aly Silva mas ele não respondeu e nem deu
importância julgo eu. No tempo da campanha para a liderança do Paigc, este
indivíduo era um fervoroso apoiante do Bá Quecuto no Facebook e a técnica que
usava era o envio de Phishing aos apoiantes do Dsp, recolhia informações
pessoais das pessoas que posteriormente eram expostas no Blog do Doka. Tentou
comigo mas não resultou. Tenham cuidado com este sujeito que está nas mãos de
B. Camara. Outra coisa, gostaria de conhecer a vossa página no Fecebook. Estamos Juntos. AC Nota GP: Até jovens inocentes,
Lesmes, Masta Tito e demais outros, os tais vendidos e comprados foram as tuas
vítimas. teu filho da puta que o bandido de Baciro Djá trouxe para Bissau para funções no aparelho de Estado e dizes que outros recebem favores.
Desde quando é que és mais honesto ou
mais competentes que os outros? Pagas e até pode ser com a tua vida para
perceberes as irresponsabilidades
dos teus actos. Publicada por O

data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13
